An ecosystem is a self-regulating unit of nature in which the living organisms of an area interact among themselves and with their non-living surroundings, exchanging materials in cycles and energy in one direction.
By the first law, energy is neither created nor destroyed — it is only converted from light to chemical to heat.
By the second law, every conversion wastes some energy as heat, so the flow is one-way (unidirectional) and never cyclic.
At every step about 90 % of the energy is lost, which is Lindeman's ten per cent law.
What is left is net primary productivity (NPP), the food actually available to consumers: Secondary productivity is the rate at which consumers store energy.

Colour contrast measured with the WCAG formula, ratio = (L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05), where L is the relative luminance of the lighter and darker colour.

Server-Side Scripting and PHP Fundamenta: Loose comparison converts types first, so the numeric strings '10' and '1e1' are equal, and null equals false.
This automatic conversion is called type juggling. == (loose equality) converts the types first and then compares the values.

Good PHP functions use type declarations, defaults and return types, pass by value unless a change is intended, and are called with strict_types on so that mistakes appear at once as errors and not as wrong results on a result sheet.
Forms, Files, Sessions and Cookies: (1) session_start() is called before any output.
MySQL for Web Applications: (b) The IBM 305 RAMAC disk unit of 1956, the first commercial hard disk, held about 5 million characters; a modern MySQL server still keeps its tables in files on a disk, only vastly larger and faster.
Connecting PHP to MySQL: The four basic database actions are called CRUD: Create (INSERT), Read (SELECT), Update (UPDATE) and Delete (DELETE).
Object-Oriented Programming in PHP: Making data private and offering methods is called encapsulation.

Nepal: First Persons, Geography, Governm: Federal parliament: House of Representatives 275 (165 first-past-the-post + 110 proportional) and National Assembly 59.
Box widths are proportional to the number of districts (77 in all); Madhesh is the southern Terai strip below Bagmati and Koshi.
Computer Fundamentals, Hardware and Soft: The CPU has the ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit), the control unit and registers; it is called the brain of the computer.

General.q: The synonym of "abundant" is
General.w: abundant means more than enough.

General.q: The antonym of "generous" is
General.w: stingy is the opposite of generous.

General.q: The synonym of "brave" is
General.w: courageous means brave.

General.q: The antonym of "ancient" is
General.w: modern is the opposite of ancient.

General.q: The synonym of "rapid" is
General.w: swift means fast.

General.q: One word for "a person who can speak two languages":
General.w: bilingual (two); a polyglot speaks many.

General.q: One word for "that which cannot be divided":
General.w: indivisible; indelible means cannot be erased.

General.q: The antonym of "victory" is
General.w: defeat is the opposite of victory.

General.q: One word for "a person who loves mankind":
General.w: philanthropist; a misanthrope hates people.

General.q: The synonym of "huge" is
General.w: enormous means very big.

General.q: The antonym of "expand" is
General.w: contract means to shrink.

General.q: One word for "a person who walks on foot":
General.w: pedestrian.

General.q: The synonym of "begin" is
General.w: commence means start.

General.q: One word for "government by the people":
General.w: democracy; autocracy is rule by one.

General.q: The present constitution of Nepal was promulgated on
General.w: 3 Ashwin 2072 (20 September 2015).

General.q: The height of Mount Everest recognised by Nepal and China is
General.w: announced in December 2020 after a joint survey.

General.q: The number of provinces in Nepal is
General.w: seven provinces.

General.q: The number of districts in Nepal is
General.w: 77 districts.

General.q: The number of local levels in Nepal is
General.w: 753 local levels.

General.q: The House of Representatives has how many members?
The first President of Nepal was
General.w: Ram Baran Yadav, 2008.

General.q: Democracy Day in Nepal is observed on
General.w: 7 Falgun marks the end of Rana rule (1951).

General.q: Nepal became a member of the United Nations in
General.w: 14 December 1955.

General.q: The national bird of Nepal is
General.w: Danphe, the Himalayan monal.

General.q: The national flower of Nepal is
General.w: rhododendron (lali guras).

General.q: The author of Muna Madan is
General.w: Laxmi Prasad Devkota.

General.q: The Aadikavi of Nepali literature is
General.w: Bhanubhakta Acharya.

General.q: The author of the novel Basain is
General.w: Lil Bahadur Chhetri.

General.q: The sum of the first five prime numbers is
General.w: 2 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 11 = 28. Option (b) 25 is what you get after dropping 2.

General.q: Which number is divisible by 9?
General.w: digit sum of 5,238 is 18, a multiple of 9. The others give 10, 17 and 16.

General.q: The product of two numbers is 2,160 and their HCF is 12. Their LCM is
The average of the first ten natural numbers is
A number leaves remainder 7 when divided by 10. The remainder on division by 5 is
General.w: N = 10q + 7 = 5(2q + 1) + 2, remainder 2.

General.q: Which of the following is a prime number?
If $n$ is an integer, which expression must be even?
General.w: n(n+1) is a product of consecutive integers. n(n+2) is odd when n is odd.

General.q: The only even prime number is
General.w: every other even number has 2 as a factor besides 1 and itself.

General.q: When Rs 56 is divided in the ratio 3: 4, the larger share is
The average of five numbers is 20. Their sum is
General.w: sum = average × number = 20 × 5 = 100.

General.q: $\frac{1}{8}$ expressed as a percentage is
Which number is divisible by 4?
General.w: the last two digits 16 are divisible by 4. 14, 02 and 18 are not.

General.q: The LCM of the co-prime numbers 7 and 9 is
General.w: co-prime numbers have LCM equal to their product, 63.

General.q: The HCF of two numbers is 8 and their LCM is 240. If one number is 48, the other is
The synonym of "ample" is
General.w: ample means plentiful.

General.q: The antonym of "rigid" is
General.w: rigid is stiff; flexible is the opposite.

General.q: One word for "a person who speaks many languages":
General.w: polyglot; bilingual is two languages.

General.q: The synonym of "tranquil" is
General.w: tranquil means calm.

General.q: One word for "a speech delivered without preparation":
General.w: extempore.

General.q: The antonym of "arrogant" is
General.w: arrogant is proud; humble is the opposite.

General.q: "To pull someone's leg" means
General.w: to joke with someone.

General.q: "A storm in a teacup" means
o: much fuss about a trivial matter
General.w: a fuss over something trivial.

General.q: The passive of "The cat chased the mouse" is
o: The mouse is chased by the cat.
The mouse was chased by the cat.
The mouse has been chased by the cat.
The cat was chased by the mouse.
General.w: simple past passive.

General.q: The passive of "Someone is repairing the road" is
General.w: present continuous passive.

General.q: Choose the correct sentence.
General.w: advice is uncountable.

General.q: Many shopkeepers are
General.w: "fourth or fifth generation".

General.q: What can a trader offer that a website cannot easily copy?
General.w: "remembers what you bought … honest advice".

General.q: The word "compete" means
General.w: compete means try to win against.

General.q: Tobacco-control legislation is an example of:
General.w: The law acts before any risk factor takes hold in the population, which is primordial prevention; vaccination (primary) and screening (secondary) act later.

General.q: Which is NOT one of the eight elements of PHC?
General.w: Transplantation is tertiary hospital care; the other three are elements named at Alma-Ata.

General.q: In a municipality of 42,000 people with a crude birth rate of 20 per 1000, the expected number of births is:
General.w: 42,000 × 20 ÷ 1000 = 840; option (c) is pregnancies (840 × 1.1) and (d) is children under five.

General.q: In the 30-cluster survey, the sampling interval for a population of 42,000 is:
General.w: 42,000 ÷ 30 = 1,400; 210 is the number of children surveyed (30 × 7).

General.q: The Nepal FCHV programme began in:
General.w: The programme started in 1988 after the 1978 PHC commitment; Astana was in 2018.

General.q: Of 1000 smokers 150 and of 2000 non-smokers 100 developed TB. The relative risk is:
General.w: Risk in smokers is 150 ÷ 1000 = 0.15 and in non-smokers 100 ÷ 2000 = 0.05, so RR = 0.15 ÷ 0.05 = 3.0.

General.q: A test has 90 true positives, 10 false negatives. Its sensitivity is:
General.w: Sensitivity = 90 ÷ (90 + 10) = 90%; 10% is the false negative rate and 80% is the specificity in the example.

General.q: If the disease becomes rarer, the PPV of a screening test will:
General.w: With fewer diseased people, a larger share of positives are false positives, so the PPV falls while sensitivity and specificity stay fixed.

General.q: The minimum sample size for a proportion with p = 0.5 and error 5% is:
The temperature range for vaccine storage is:
General.w: Vaccines are kept between +2 and +8 °C; below 0 °C freeze-sensitive vaccines lose potency, and above 8 °C all lose it.

General.q: A health post uses 840 BCG doses with 50% wastage. Doses to order are:
General.w: Wastage factor = 1 ÷ (1 - 0.5) = 2, so 840 × 2 = 1,680 doses (84 vials of 20).

General.q: A Breteau index measures:
General.w: BI is positive containers per 100 houses; the house index is the percentage of houses with larvae.

General.q: Fast breathing in a child aged 14 months is:
General.w: The cut-off for 12-59 months is 40 breaths a minute; 50 applies to 2-11 months and 60 to infants under 2 months.

General.q: A MUAC of 112 mm in a child of 2 years means:
General.w: Below 115 mm is severe acute malnutrition and needs RUTF or referral.

General.q: The Nepal Nursing Council Act was passed in:
General.w: The NNC Act 2052 (1996) created the Council. 2042 and 2062 are distractors; 2072 is the year of the 2015 earthquake era, unrelated.

General.q: Refusing to share a patient's HIV status with the neighbour is:
General.w: Confidentiality means protecting private health information. Veracity is truth-telling to the patient, not secrecy from others.

General.q: A nurse who teaches ORS preparation to a mother is acting mainly as:
General.w: Teaching is the educator role. A manager organises resources, a researcher collects data and a counsellor supports feelings.

General.q: The first School of Nursing in Nepal opened in:
General.w: The School of Nursing started in 1956. 1952 is when two women were sent abroad to train, and 1972 is the move to TU.

General.q: The second step of the nursing process is:
General.w: Diagnosis follows assessment. Planning is third and evaluation is last.

General.q: A Braden score of 11 means:
General.w: 10-12 is high risk. 9 or less is very high and 13-14 is moderate.

General.q: The best-written outcome is:
o: patient will walk 20 metres with a walker by day 5
General.w: It is specific, measurable and time-bound, and it is about the patient. (c) is a nurse action; (a) and (d) are vague.

General.q: Stage 3 pressure injury shows:
General.w: Stage 3 is full-thickness skin loss with visible fat. Bone exposure is stage 4.

General.q: A BP cuff that is too narrow gives:
General.w: A narrow cuff needs more pressure to compress the artery, so the reading is too high. A wide cuff gives a low reading.

General.q: MAP for BP 90/60 mmHg is:
General.w: (90 + 2 × 60) ÷ 3 = 70. The other numbers are arithmetic slips such as adding without doubling the diastolic.

General.q: A patient opens eyes to voice, is confused and localises pain. GCS is:
General.w: E3 + V4 + M5 = 12. The patient is moderately impaired.

General.q: To make 0.5% chlorine from 5% liquid bleach, the dilution is:
General.w: 5 ÷ 0.5 = 10 total parts, i.e. 1 part bleach and 9 parts water. 1:4 gives 1%, 1:49 gives 0.1%.

General.q: PPE is removed in the order:
General.w: The most contaminated items (gloves, then goggles, then gown) go first and the mask last, then hands are washed.

General.q: A 20 drops/mL set, 1000 mL over 8 hours, runs at about:
General.w: 1000 × 20 ÷ 480 = 41.67, rounded to 42. 83 is the rate for a 4-hour run, and 21 for a 16-hour run.

General.q: The Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase moves:
General.w: The pump uses ATP to remove 3 Na⁺ and bring in 2 K⁺, keeping the inside negative. The other options reverse the direction.

General.q: With HCO₃⁻ 24 mmol/L and PaCO₂ 40 mmHg, the pH is:
General.w: pH = 6.1 + log 20 = 7.40. Values of 7.20 or 7.30 are acidotic.

General.q: Warfarin therapy is monitored by:
General.w: Warfarin depresses vitamin K clotting factors, which the extrinsic pathway (PT/INR) reflects; aPTT monitors heparin.

General.q: Tetanus immunoglobulin gives:
General.w: It is ready-made antibody given from outside, so it is passive and artificial.

General.q: The normal pacemaker of the heart is the:
General.w: The SA node has the fastest intrinsic rate (60-100/min), so it controls the heart; the AV node (40-60) and Purkinje fibres (20-40) only take over on failure.

General.q: On an ECG, R-R is 4 large squares. The heart rate is:
General.w: 300 ÷ 4 = 75/min. A value of 150 would need an R-R of 2 large squares.

General.q: The first heart sound is produced by closure of the:
General.w: S1 ("lub") is closure of the mitral and tricuspid valves as the ventricles begin to contract; S2 is closure of the semilunar valves.

General.q: ACE inhibitors lower BP by blocking the formation of:
General.w: ACE converts angiotensin I to angiotensin II, a strong vasoconstrictor; blocking it lowers vascular tone and aldosterone release.

General.q: The bronchus into which a foreign body most often enters is:
General.w: The right main bronchus is shorter, wider and more vertical, so aspirated material and misplaced tubes enter it.

General.q: Tidal volume 500 mL, dead space 150 mL and rate 14/min give an alveolar ventilation of:
General.w: (500 - 150) × 14 = 4900 mL/min. 7000 mL/min is the minute ventilation, which ignores dead space.

General.q: pH 7.30, PaCO₂ 30 and HCO₃⁻ 14 mmol/L represent:
General.w: Both pH and HCO₃⁻ are low (metabolic acidosis); the low PaCO₂ is the compensation (Winter's value 29).

General.q: A right shift of the oxyhaemoglobin curve is caused by:
General.w: Acid, heat and high CO₂ lower haemoglobin affinity so oxygen is unloaded in active tissues; the other options cause a left shift.

General.q: FEV₁/FVC of 50% suggests:
General.w: A ratio below 70% means airflow obstruction, as in COPD or asthma; restrictive disease keeps the ratio normal.

General.q: Intrinsic factor, needed for vitamin B12 absorption, is secreted by:
General.w: Parietal cells make HCl and intrinsic factor; chief cells make pepsinogen and mucous cells make mucus.

General.q: A patient with E2, V3, M4 has a GCS of:
General.w: 2 + 3 + 4 = 9, a moderate head injury; the airway should be watched closely since the score is near 8.

General.q: The structure that joins the two cerebral hemispheres is the:
General.w: The corpus callosum is the large white-matter bridge seen as an arch in the sagittal MRI; the thalamus is a relay, and the pons is in the brainstem.

General.q: In primary hypothyroidism the usual pattern is:
General.w: When the thyroid fails, T4 is low, so feedback no longer holds TSH down and TSH is high. Low TSH with low T4 points to a pituitary cause.

General.q: The hormone that raises blood glucose is:
General.w: Glucagon from alpha cells breaks down liver glycogen. Insulin lowers glucose, and ADH and calcitonin act on water and calcium.

General.q: Na 132, Cl 96 and HCO₃ 8 mmol/L give an anion gap of:
General.w: 132 - (96 + 8) = 28, a high gap that shows unmeasured ketone acids; the normal gap is 8-12.

General.q: After thyroidectomy the nurse watches for tingling around the mouth because of:
General.w: The parathyroids may be damaged or removed, PTH falls and calcium drops; mouth tingling and a positive Chvostek's sign are early signs.

General.q: Most glucose reabsorption occurs in the:
General.w: The proximal tubule reabsorbs all filtered glucose through sodium-linked carriers; glucose appears in urine only when blood glucose passes about 180 mg/dL.

General.q: The hormone that makes the collecting duct permeable to water is:
General.w: ADH inserts aquaporin channels in the collecting duct. Aldosterone acts on sodium, renin is an enzyme and ANP promotes sodium loss.

General.q: A 70 kg adult needs maintenance fluid by the 4-2-1 rule of:
General.w: 40 + 20 + 50 = 110 mL/h. Option (d) would be 2 mL/kg/h for the whole weight.

General.q: A peaked T wave and wide QRS suggest:
General.w: High potassium reduces the resting potential and gives tall peaked T waves, then wide QRS and arrest; low potassium gives flat T waves and U waves.

General.q: Ovulation in a 32-day cycle occurs on about day:
General.w: The luteal phase is fixed at about 14 days, so ovulation is on day 32 - 14 = 18. Day 14 applies only to a 28-day cycle.

General.q: The hormone detected by the urine pregnancy test is:
General.w: hCG comes from the trophoblast soon after implantation. FSH and LH peak at ovulation and progesterone is not used in the strip test.

General.q: Fertilisation normally occurs in the:
General.w: The egg is fertilised in the ampulla, the widest part of the tube, and the embryo then travels to the uterus.

General.q: The cells that remove bone are:
General.w: Osteoclasts resorb bone, osteoblasts form it, osteocytes maintain it and chondrocytes are cartilage cells.

General.q: A man weighs 70 kg and is 1.75 m tall. His BMI is:
General.w: 70 ÷ 1.75² = 22.9 kg/m², which is normal by WHO but at the upper normal for Asian risk (23 is the cut-off for overweight).

General.q: A woman who weighed 60 kg now weighs 54 kg; her weight loss is:
General.w: (60 - 54) ÷ 60 × 100 = 10%; dividing by the present weight would give 11%, which is wrong.

General.q: The amino-acid pairing that makes rice and dal a complete protein is explained by:
o: cereals low in lysine and pulses low in methionine
General.w: Each food is low in a different amino acid, so together they complete each other; this is why Nepali dal bhat and sarbottam pitho work.

General.q: A pregnant woman has haemoglobin 8.6 g/dL; the anaemia is:
General.w: In pregnancy Hb 7-9.9 is moderate, 10-10.9 mild and below 7 severe; she needs treatment doses, a check for causes and follow-up.

General.q: A 6-kg child with SAM treated at home needs RUTF of 200 kcal/kg/day. The number of 500-kcal sachets daily is:
General.w: 200 × 6 = 1,200 kcal ÷ 500 = 2.4 sachets; (c) is for a 7.5-kg child. Dose is always calculated from the present weight.

General.q: A child of 5.0 kg whose reference median is 8.0 kg has a weight-for-age of:
General.w: 5.0 ÷ 8.0 × 100 = 62.5%, moderate by Gomez (60-74%); the 37.5% answer wrongly divides the median by the weight.

General.q: The most important sign that separates kwashiorkor from marasmus is:
General.w: Bilateral pitting oedema defines kwashiorkor; wasting and low weight occur in both and a poor appetite is common to both.

General.q: The glycaemic load of a portion with GI 73 and 30 g carbohydrate is:
General.w: GL = 73 × 30 ÷ 100 = 21.9; GL combines the quality (GI) and quantity of carbohydrate.

General.q: A 50-kg patient at high risk of refeeding syndrome should begin at about:
General.w: Refeeding risk requires 10 kcal/kg (or less), so 50 × 10 = 500 kcal at first, with thiamine; full feeding may cause fatal hypophosphataemia.

General.q: The most reliable bedside check of NG tube position is:
o: listening for air over the stomach
the patient being able to talk.
General.w: A gastric aspirate pH of 5.5 or less (or X-ray) is the accepted check; sound of air and ease of flushing can occur with the tube in the lung.

General.q: The count of instruments, swabs and needles is confirmed at:
General.w: The sign out is the last pause before the patient leaves, and it is the time to find a missing swab while the wound can still be opened.

General.q: A man who smoked 20 bidi a day for 25 years has:
General.w: 20 bidi is one pack, so 1 × 25 = 25 pack-years; (c) wrongly treats each year as 2 packs.

General.q: A patient with PEFR 200 L/min whose predicted value is 400 L/min is at:
General.w: 200 ÷ 400 × 100 = 50%: yellow-red border, treat as an acute attack; (a) inverts the ratio.

General.q: PaO2 80 mmHg on an FiO2 of 0.40 gives a PaO2/FiO2 ratio of:
General.w: 80 ÷ 0.40 = 200; a ratio below 300 shows impaired gas exchange.

General.q: The SpO2 target for a COPD patient who retains CO2 is:
General.w: In chronic CO2 retention, high oxygen removes the hypoxic drive and CO2 rises; keep 88-92% with a Venturi mask.

General.q: The MAP of a patient with BP 120/80 is:
General.w: (120 + 2 × 80) ÷ 3 = 93.3; (c) is the simple average of 120 and 80, which ignores the longer diastole.

General.q: The heart rate with 6 large squares between R waves is:
General.w: 300 ÷ 6 = 50 per minute; 75 would need 4 large squares.

General.q: Serum albumin 2.8 g/dL and ascitic albumin 0.9 g/dL give a SAAG of:
General.w: 2.8 - 0.9 = 1.9, so the ascites is caused by portal hypertension (SAAG 1.1 or more).

General.q: In hepatic encephalopathy the drug given to produce 2-3 soft stools a day is:
General.w: Lactulose acidifies the colon, traps ammonia and speeds transit; furosemide treats fluid, and loperamide or morphine slow the gut and worsen encephalopathy.

General.q: A WBC of 3,000 with 10% neutrophils gives an ANC of:
General.w: 3,000 × 10 ÷ 100 = 300, which is severe neutropenia (below 500); (d) uses the lymphocyte percentage.

General.q: The first action when a transfusion reaction is suspected is:
General.w: Stopping the transfusion limits the dose of incompatible or contaminated blood; drugs and calls follow, and increasing the rate is dangerous.

General.q: Which of the following best describes the scope of practice for an adult nurse?
o: Providing care exclusively in pediatric settings for children aged 0-18 years old.
Administering care in critical care units for patients requiring life support systems.
Offering primary and specialized healthcare services to adults, including preventive care, diagnosis, and treatment.
Managing administrative tasks within hospitals and healthcare centers without direct patient care.
General.w: Adult nurses provide care specifically tailored to the adult population, including a range of health services from prevention to treatment.

General.q: According to the Nursing Act, what is required for a nurse to legally practice in Nepal?
o: A valid driving license and a certificate in emergency first aid.
Registration with the Nursing Council of Nepal (NCN) and possession of a valid practicing license.
A bachelor’s degree in any field and a minimum of two years experience in any hospital.
A recommendation letter from a practicing physician and certification in medical ethics.
General.w: Legal practice as a nurse in Nepal requires registration with NCN and holding a valid practicing license.

General.q: What does the principle of non-maleficence in nursing ethics imply?
o: Ensuring that healthcare professionals receive fair wages for their work.
Providing the best possible care and treatment to all patients without discrimination.
Avoiding actions that could cause harm to the patient and preventing harm where possible.
Promoting health education and community health improvement initiatives.
General.w: Non-maleficence is about avoiding harm, which is crucial in nursing practice.

General.q: Urea falls from 120 to 30 mg/dL in dialysis. The URR is:
General.w: (120 - 30) ÷ 120 × 100 = 75%; 90 is the difference in mg/dL, not a percentage, and 25% is the proportion left.

General.q: Before starting dialysis you cannot feel the thrill in the fistula. The first action is to:
o: start dialysis in the other arm
inform the doctor at once and do not use the access
apply a warm pack and wait.
General.w: A missing thrill means that the fistula has clotted; forcing a needle in or waiting wastes the access that took months to mature, so tell the doctor and arrange a catheter or an angioplasty.

General.q: A patient has sodium 140, chloride 104 and bicarbonate 24 mmol/L. The anion gap is:
General.w: 140 - (104 + 24) = 12, which is normal (8-12); 28 would be the answer in DKA.

General.q: A 60 kg patient in DKA is ordered insulin at 0.1 unit/kg/h. The rate is:
General.w: 0.1 × 60 = 6 units/h; (b) uses 0.05 unit/kg/h and (d) forgets the factor of 0.1.

General.q: In DKA the correct order of treatment is:
o: fluids, insulin with potassium monitoring, then find the cause
General.w: Dehydration is the first danger, so fluids start first; insulin goes on after the first fluid and a potassium check, and bicarbonate is rarely needed; oral sugar worsens ketoacidosis.

General.q: A patient opens the eyes to voice (3), is confused (4) and localises pain (5). The GCS is:
General.w: E3 + V4 + M5 = 12; 15 is a fully alert person and 9 would need a lower motor score.

General.q: MAP 90 mmHg and ICP 20 mmHg give a CPP of:
General.w: CPP = MAP - ICP = 90 - 20 = 70 mmHg, which is in the target range of 60-70 or more; 110 forgets to subtract.

General.q: WBC 3,000 per mm³ with 20% neutrophils gives an ANC of:
General.w: 3,000 × 20% = 600; this is just above the severe cut-off of 500, so the risk of infection is high; 60 forgets the factor of 10.

General.q: A woman is 150 cm tall and weighs 54 kg. Her BSA by the Mosteller formula is:
General.w: √(150 × 54 ÷ 3600) = √2.25 = 1.5 m²; 2.25 is the value before taking the square root.

General.q: A patient on chemotherapy has a temperature of 38.5 °C and a low neutrophil count. The first priority is:
o: blood cultures and IV antibiotics within 1 hour
wait for the next clinic day
General.w: Neutropenic fever is sepsis until proved otherwise and mortality rises each hour without antibiotics; paracetamol alone masks the fever and delay is dangerous.

General.q: What is the primary purpose of conducting a comprehensive health assessment in adult nursing?
o: To identify the patient's favorite activities
To evaluate the patient's financial status for billing purposes
To determine the patient's physical, psychological, and social health status
To prescribe medication without further consultation
General.w: The primary purpose is to get a holistic view of the patient's health.

General.q: Which of the following is a key component of effective communication in adult nursing?
o: Using medical jargon to demonstrate expertise
Avoiding eye contact to maintain professionalism
Minimizing the time spent on patient interaction to see more patients
General.w: Active listening and appropriate response are essential for effective communication.

General.q: In the context of pain management, what does the acronym PQRST stand for?
o: Pain Quality, Radiation, Severity, Timing, Trigger
General.w: PQRST is used to assess pain characteristics in patients.

General.q: When teaching a patient about wound care, which of the following is crucial to emphasize?
o: The importance of changing the dressing according to the schedule provided
The need to keep the wound moist at all times
The effectiveness of applying ice directly to the wound
The requirement to use alcohol for cleaning the wound daily
General.w: Following the prescribed dressing change schedule is vital for proper wound healing.

General.q: An 80-year-old man weighs 60 kg and has a serum creatinine of 1.2 mg/dL. His Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance is about:
General.w: (140 - 80) × 60 ÷ (72 × 1.2) = 41.7 mL/min; 0.7 leaves out the weight and 100 ignores age.

General.q: The best single predictor of an older person's future independence is:
General.w: Function (ADL, gait speed, grip) predicts disability, hospital stay and death better than age alone; the other options have no direct link.

General.q: A patient has a history of falling (25), a secondary diagnosis (15), an IV line (20) and impaired gait (20). His Morse score is:
General.w: 25 + 15 + 20 + 20 = 80, high risk (45 or more); 45 is only the cut-off and 100 adds an item not present.

General.q: A patient's BP is 150/80 lying and 124/76 standing at 3 minutes. The systolic drop is:
General.w: 150 - 124 = 26 mmHg, which is 20 or more; 4 mmHg is the diastolic difference misread, and options (c) and (d) are wrong arithmetic or interpretation.

General.q: You find an older patient on the ward floor. The first action is:
o: assess consciousness, breathing and injury before moving
tie the patient to the bed.
General.w: Moving a patient with a neck, hip or head injury can worsen it; assess first, then lift with help. Restraint is unsafe and unethical.

General.q: The typical leg position in a displaced femoral neck fracture is:
General.w: The unopposed muscles pull the distal fragment up and rotate it outward, so the leg looks shorter and turned out.

General.q: A screening test is positive in 36 of 40 people who have dementia. Its sensitivity is:
General.w: Sensitivity = true positives ÷ all diseased = 36 ÷ 40 = 90%; 36% is the count and 4% is the false-negative fraction.

General.q: Donepezil 10 mg a day is given as 5 mg tablets for 28 days. The number of tablets is:
General.w: 10 mg needs two 5-mg tablets a day, so 2 × 28 = 56 tablets; 28 would give only 5 mg a day.

General.q: An 80-year-old becomes drowsy and inattentive over one day. This is most consistent with:
General.w: Acute onset with inattention and altered awareness defines delirium, an emergency; dementia and depression do not start in a day.

General.q: An 80-year-old man weighs 70 kg and his creatinine is 1.0 mg/dL. His Cockcroft-Gault clearance is about:
General.w: (140 - 80) × 70 ÷ (72 × 1.0) = 58.3 mL/min; 41.7 uses a weight of 50 kg and 100 ignores age.

General.q: Diazepam has a half-life of 80 h in an 80-year-old. The days to steady state (5 half-lives) are:
General.w: 5 × 80 ÷ 24 = 16.7 days; 3.3 days is for a half-life of 16 h and 33.3 multiplies by ten.

General.q: 250 mL is ordered over 4 hours with a 20 drops/mL set. The rate is:
General.w: 250 × 20 ÷ 240 = 21 gtt/min; 10 and 15 use the wrong drop factor or time, and 42 is the rate for 500 mL.

General.q: Under the 2023 Beers criteria the recommendation for starting aspirin to prevent a first heart attack in a 75-year-old is to:
General.w: Evidence shows more bleeding than benefit in older adults who have not had a heart or stroke event; those already taking it should be reviewed by the doctor.

General.q: A patient has Braden items 3, 3, 2, 2, 3 and 2. The total and risk level are:
General.w: 3 + 3 + 2 + 2 + 3 + 2 = 15, which is in the mild risk band of 15-18; 9 would be very high risk and 18 is still at risk.

General.q: In Selye's GAS the stage in which the body adapts and hormone levels stay high is:
General.w: Alarm is the first reaction, exhaustion is the failure of adaptation; resistance is the stage of high-level coping.

General.q: A person with a sudden earthquake loss of home and family is in which type of crisis?
General.w: A disaster that is not part of life and affects many people is adventitious; maturational crises are predictable and situational crises are personal events.

General.q: The most important first nursing action for a person in crisis is:
General.w: Safety first, because a person in danger cannot use advice or counselling; sleeping tablets alone only hide the problem.

General.q: Which statement about Kübler-Ross's stages is correct?
o: people may move back and forth
acceptance must be reached in a month.
General.w: The stages are not fixed or time-bound and apply to family also; (a), (b) and (d) are the common errors.

General.q: Rubbing a bumped knee relieves pain mainly because:
o: large touch fibres close the gate
General.w: Large A-beta fibres close the dorsal-horn gate (Melzack and Wall); C fibres are not destroyed and adrenaline is not the mechanism.

General.q: Before giving morphine the nurse finds a respiratory rate of 8 per minute and a drowsy patient. The correct action is:
o: hold the dose and inform the doctor
General.w: A respiratory rate below 10 with sedation signals opioid toxicity, so hold the drug and call; a half dose still depresses breathing.

General.q: The MAP for a BP of 120/80 mmHg is:
General.w: (120 + 2 × 80) ÷ 3 = 93.3; 100 uses a simple average; 40 is the pulse pressure.

General.q: A nurse counts 14 breaths in 30 seconds. The respiratory rate is:
General.w: 14 × 2 = 28 breaths a minute, which is fast; 14 is only a half-minute count.

General.q: A woman of 60 kg and 1.5 m has a BMI of:
General.w: 60 ÷ 2.25 = 26.7; 20.0 forgets to square the height.

General.q: Which technique comes before palpation in an abdominal examination?
General.w: Auscultation comes before percussion and palpation in the abdomen because touch can change bowel sounds.

General.q: A patient says "ho, ho" but cannot repeat the instruction. The best nursing action is:
o: use simple words, a picture or interpreter and teach-back
General.w: A nod is not understanding; teach-back and clear channels confirm it. Louder speech does not help a language gap.

General.q: Scutari mortality fell from 42.7% to 2.2%. The relative reduction is about:
General.w: (42.7 - 2.2) ÷ 42.7 = 94.8%; 40.5 is the absolute fall in percentage points and 5.2% is the leftover share.

General.q: In Neuman's model the outermost ring that is first met by stressors is:
General.w: The flexible line is the outer protective buffer; the others lie inside it.

General.q: Immunising a child before exposure is which Neuman level?
General.w: Strengthening defences before the stressor is primary prevention; secondary treats early disease and tertiary rehabilitates.

General.q: In a survey of 9,200 adults, 4.3% have a current mental disorder. The number of people is about:
General.w: 9,200 × 0.043 = 395.6, about 396; 920 is the lifetime count (10%) and 92 is 1%.

General.q: The phase in which the patient actively uses the nurse's help to solve problems is:
General.w: In exploitation the patient uses the services offered; orientation is the meeting, identification the naming of problems and resolution the ending.

General.q: A patient on 15-minute observation is checked how many times in 24 hours:
General.w: 1,440 minutes ÷ 15 = 96 checks; 48 would be every 30 minutes.

General.q: Which statement about mental health law in Nepal is correct:
o: a Mental Health Act of 2052 governs all admissions
there is no standalone Mental Health Act; Section 185 of the Criminal Code punishes abetting suicide
suicide attempts are punished by prison
General.w: Nepal still has no standalone act; the Criminal Code 2074 section 185 targets abetment, and an attempt is treated as a health problem.

General.q: A patient's weight rises from 62 to 67 kg on olanzapine. The gain is about:
General.w: (67 - 62) ÷ 62 × 100 = 8.1%, above the 7% threshold; 5 kg alone is not the percentage.

General.q: A patient on fluphenazine decanoate every 2 weeks receives how many injections in a year:
General.w: 52 weeks ÷ 2 = 26; every 4 weeks would give 13.

General.q: A patient given haloperidol twists the neck and the eyes roll upward on day 2. The first response is:
o: stop all drugs for a week
call the doctor and give an IM anticholinergic as ordered
General.w: This is acute dystonia, treated quickly with an anticholinergic; more haloperidol worsens it and reassurance alone does not stop the spasm.

General.q: Lithium carbonate 900 mg/day is given as 300 mg tablets for 14 days. The tablets needed are:
General.w: 900 ÷ 300 = 3 tablets a day, 3 × 14 = 42; 28 would be only 2 tablets a day.

General.q: A woman screened with PHQ-9 gives item 9 a score of 1. The next step is:
o: ask directly about suicide today and assess risk
General.w: Any positive item 9 needs a direct suicide enquiry the same day; asking does not raise risk.

General.q: After an earthquake, the first step for a frightened survivor is:
o: a safe place, basic needs and psychological first aid
General.w: Safety, basic needs and psychological first aid come first; forced debriefing and routine sedatives can harm and delay recovery.

General.q: After rapid tranquillisation, observations every 15 minutes in the first hour number:
General.w: 60 ÷ 15 = 4 checks of breathing, BP, pulse, SpO2 and consciousness.

General.q: In suspected Wernicke encephalopathy in an alcohol-dependent patient, the correct order is:
General.w: Glucose alone uses up the remaining thiamine and can precipitate or worsen Wernicke encephalopathy, so thiamine is given first or together.

General.q: What is the primary focus of psychiatric nursing?
o: Providing care for individuals with mental health disorders
Managing chronic diseases like diabetes and hypertension
General.w: Psychiatric nursing focuses specifically on mental health disorders.

General.q: In the context of psychiatric nursing, what does the term 'delirium' refer to?
o: A state of prolonged unconsciousness from which the patient cannot be aroused
A type of severe depression characterized by loss of interest in activities
A condition characterized by sudden confusion and changes in attention
A disorder characterized by alternating episodes of euphoria and depression
General.w: Delirium refers to a sudden onset of confusion and changes in attention.

General.q: The term "sociology" was first used by:
General.w: Auguste Comte coined the word in 1838 and called it the science of society. Durkheim, Weber and Marx developed the field later, so they are not first users of the term.

General.q: In a village of two equal groups (50% each) the Simpson diversity index is:
General.w: The index is 1 - (0.25 + 0.25) = 0.50. It would be 0 if there were one group only and it rises as groups multiply and become more equal; 1.0 is never reached exactly.

General.q: Disrespect to the dead body of a family elder, strongly condemned by the community, is a breach of:
General.w: Respect for the dead carries moral weight and strong disapproval, which defines a more. A folkway is a mild everyday custom, and a fashion has no moral weight.

General.q: A nurse who is also a mother and is called for night duty on the night her child is ill faces:
General.w: Two roles (mother and nurse) make incompatible demands at the same time, which is role conflict. Role strain is stress inside one role, such as an overloaded nurse.

General.q: According to Census 2021, the Hindu share of Nepal's population is about:
General.w: The 2021 census recorded 81.19% Hindu, with Buddhists at 8.21% and Muslims at 5.09%. The figures of 91%, 71% and 61% do not match any census.

General.q: A family in which several married brothers live with their wives and children under one head and one kitchen is:
General.w: A joint family has several couples of related men under one authority and one kitchen. A nuclear family has only parents and children, and an extended family does not necessarily share one head or kitchen.

General.q: The legal minimum age of marriage in Nepal is:
General.w: The Civil Code sets 20 years for both sexes, with consent. Earlier rules of 18 and 16 are obsolete, so options (a), (b) and (d) are wrong.

General.q: If the richest 20% hold 47% and the poorest 20% hold 6% of income, the quintile ratio is about:
General.w: The ratio is 47 / 6 = 7.8; 0.1 is the inverse and 41 is the difference. A ratio of 1 would mean equality.

General.q: Which statement about caste is correct?
o: Discrimination is a crime under the 2011 Act
General.w: The Caste-Based Discrimination and Untouchability Act 2068 (2011) and Article 24 of the 2015 Constitution forbid it. Caste is a closed system, dates from the Muluki Ain of 1854 or earlier, and strongly affects health.

General.q: The first psychology laboratory was set up in 1879 by:
General.w: Wilhelm Wundt opened the Leipzig laboratory in 1879. Freud founded psychoanalysis, Pavlov studied conditioned reflexes and Skinner studied operant behaviour.

General.q: A child with mental age 10 years and chronological age 12 years has a ratio IQ of about:
General.w: Ratio IQ = 10 / 12 x 100 = 83.3. 100 would need equal ages, and 120 would mean the mental age is above the chronological age.

General.q: A Wechsler score with z = -2.5 gives a deviation IQ of:
General.w: Deviation IQ = 100 + 15 x (-2.5) = 62.5. 77.5 would be z = -1.5, and 85 would be z = -1.

General.q: A child who fears the white coat after painful injections shows:
General.w: The white coat (neutral) was paired with the painful needle (unconditioned), so the coat alone now causes fear. Operant learning depends on consequences of behaviour, not on pairing of stimuli.

General.q: The experiment in which subjects judged line lengths against a majority was done by:
General.w: Solomon Asch used line cards and confederates. Milgram studied obedience with shocks, Zimbardo studied roles in a mock prison and Bandura studied observational learning.

General.q: A 5-year-old weighs 13.5 kg; the reference median is 17.0 kg and the SD is 1.5 kg. The z-score is:
General.w: (13.5 - 17.0) ÷ 1.5 = -2.3, below -2, so she is underweight. -1.2 is within the normal band.

General.q: Ninety children need one dose of MR in a session and the wastage rate for the 10-dose vial is 40%. The doses to issue are:
General.w: 90 ÷ (1 - 0.4) = 150 doses = 15 vials. Ordering only 90 doses leaves the last 60 children unvaccinated because open vials are discarded after 6 hours.

General.q: Penta1 was given to 200 infants and Penta3 to 170. The dropout rate is:
General.w: (200 - 170) ÷ 200 = 15%. Dropout above 10% is considered high and needs defaulter tracing.

General.q: Which vaccine is given intradermally in the right upper arm at 14 weeks and 9 months in Nepal?
General.w: fIPV is 0.1 mL intradermal in the right upper arm. PCV is IM in the thigh, MR is subcutaneous in the left arm and TCV is IM in the left thigh.

General.q: A baby weighed 3.2 kg at birth and 2.9 kg on day 3. The weight loss is:
General.w: (3.2 - 2.9) ÷ 3.2 = 9.4%. This is at the upper limit of the normal 5-10%; check feeding and watch for more loss. 3% and 6% are wrong calculations and 15% would be dangerous.

General.q: At 24 hours the right hand SpO₂ is 96% and the foot is 94%. The screen is:
General.w: Both readings are 95% or more and the difference (2 points) is not above 3, so the screen is passed. A fail needs a value below 95% or a difference above 3.

General.q: A scalp swelling that is not present at birth, appears on day 2 and does not cross the suture lines is:
General.w: A cephalhaematoma is bleeding under the periosteum and is limited by the suture lines. A caput is present at birth and crosses sutures.

General.q: A child with SAM weighs 8 kg and needs 175 kcal/kg/day from RUTF (500 kcal per sachet). The sachets per day:
General.w: 175 × 8 = 1,400 kcal ÷ 500 = 2.8 sachets. Giving 2 sachets under-feeds the child and slows recovery.

General.q: A 14-month-old has a cough, respiratory rate 42 a minute, no chest indrawing and no danger signs. The IMNCI classification is:
General.w: At 12-59 months a rate of 40 or more is fast breathing, so this is pneumonia (yellow) treated at home with amoxicillin. It would be severe only if a danger sign or SpO₂ below 90% were present.

General.q: A child has a MUAC of 11.2 cm and no oedema. This is:
General.w: A MUAC below 11.5 cm is SAM even without oedema. MAM is 11.5 to below 12.5 cm.

General.q: The attack rate is 10% in the unvaccinated and 2% in the vaccinated. Vaccine efficacy is:
General.w: (10 - 2) ÷ 10 = 80%. VE is the proportion of cases prevented, not the vaccinated attack rate.

General.q: For a disease with R₀ of 12, the herd-immunity threshold is about:
General.w: 1 - 1/12 = 0.917. A higher R₀ needs a higher immune fraction, so measles needs over 92%.

General.q: The modern CPR is 40% and the total demand is 80%. The demand satisfied by modern methods is:
General.w: 40 ÷ 80 = 50%. 40% is the CPR itself and 80% is the demand, not the share met.

General.q: How many 200 microgram tablets make a misoprostol dose of 800 micrograms?
General.w: 800 ÷ 200 = 4 tablets. Two tablets give only 400 micrograms and would risk an incomplete abortion.

General.q: CPR is 57% and total demand is 78%. The unmet need is:
General.w: Total demand = CPR + unmet need, so 78 - 57 = 21%. 43% is the modern method use.

General.q: Under the Safe Motherhood and Reproductive Health Rights Act 2075, whose consent is needed for abortion at 10 weeks?
General.w: The Act requires only the woman's own consent up to 12 weeks. Husband or parent consent is not needed, and a court order is not part of the process.

General.q: A health post issued 600 condoms in a year. The CYP is:
General.w: 600 ÷ 120 = 5. 6 divides by 100 instead of 120.

General.q: A health post gave 60 DMPA doses in a year. The CYP is:
General.w: 60 ÷ 4 = 15; each woman needs 4 doses a year. 240 multiplies instead of dividing.

General.q: The shortest cycle is 27 days. By the Ogino-Knaus rule the first fertile day is:
General.w: 27 - 18 = 9. 7 and 12 do not follow the rule.

General.q: Of 1,000 women using the pill in typical use for a year, the expected pregnancies are:
General.w: 7% of 1,000 = 70. 14 is 7 per 500 and 130 is the male condom figure.

General.q: Which woman should NOT be given a combined pill?
o: Age 22, on antibiotics for a sore throat.
General.w: Blood pressure of 160/100 mmHg or more makes the pill category 4 (risk of stroke). The others are category 1 or 2.

General.q: A woman weighs 78 kg and is 1.60 m tall. Her BMI is:
General.w: 78 ÷ 2.56 = 30.5, obese class I. 24.4 is from 62 kg; 48.8 forgets to square the height.

General.q: A woman has regular 32-day cycles. Ovulation is expected around day:
General.w: 32 - 14 = 18. Day 14 applies only to a 28-day cycle; the luteal phase stays near 14 days.

General.q: The chance of pregnancy is 25% each cycle. The cumulative chance in 6 cycles is about:
General.w: 1 - 0.75⁶ = 0.822. Adding 25% six times gives 150%, which is impossible, so chances must be multiplied.

General.q: BMD is 0.70, the young adult mean 1.00 and the SD 0.10. The T-score is:
General.w: (0.70 - 1.00) ÷ 0.10 = -3.0, which is osteoporosis. -1.0 would be normal and -2.0 would be osteopenia.

General.q: A test finds 45 of 50 women with disease. Its sensitivity is:
General.w: 45 ÷ 50 = 90%; sensitivity looks only at women who have the disease. 95% is wrongly 45 ÷ 47.

General.q: A woman with a 40-day cycle probably ovulates on day:
General.w: Ovulation = cycle length - 14 = 26, because the luteal phase is fixed at 14 days; day 14 is correct only for a 28-day cycle.

General.q: The vessel that carries the most oxygenated blood to the baby is the:
General.w: The single umbilical vein carries oxygenated blood from the placenta (about 80% saturated); the arteries carry deoxygenated blood away from the baby.

General.q: A woman in her third pregnancy has two living term children. Her GTPAL is:
General.w: Gravida counts the present pregnancy (3), two were term (T2) and none preterm or aborted; (b) forgets the present one.

General.q: Hegar's sign is:
o: softening of the isthmus of the uterus
a dark midline on the abdomen.
General.w: Hegar's sign is a soft compressible isthmus at 6-8 weeks (probable sign); (a) is Chadwick's, (c) is a positive sign and (d) a presumptive skin sign.

General.q: For heartburn in the third trimester the best advice is:
o: small frequent meals and raised head
General.w: Small meals and an upright position reduce reflux; lying flat worsens it, and iron should continue, with food, for anaemia.

General.q: In a ward with 500 expected births, 350 women completed four ANC visits. The coverage is:
The mean arterial pressure for 150/100 mmHg is:
General.w: (150 + 2 × 100) ÷ 3 = 116.7; adding without doubling the diastolic gives wrong answers.

General.q: Before each maintenance dose of magnesium sulfate the nurse must check all EXCEPT:
General.w: Magnesium toxicity shows as low respiratory rate, absent knee reflex and low urine; blood sugar is not part of the check.

General.q: A woman has stayed at 7 cm for 3 hours. The Labour Care Guide advises:
o: reassess and decide on the cause
General.w: The LCG threshold for 7 cm is 3 hours; reaching it prompts reassessment of the woman, baby, contractions and descent, not automatic surgery.

General.q: Bishop score with dilatation 3 cm, effacement 50%, station -2, medium consistency and mid-position is:
General.w: Scores 2 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 6, an unfavourable cervix for induction (8 or more is favourable).

General.q: Oxytocin for prevention of PPH is given as:
o: 10 IU IM within 1 minute of birth
General.w: WHO recommends oxytocin 10 IU IM within one minute of birth; the oral route does not work and waiting for the placenta wastes the key minutes.

General.q: A baby born at 3,500 g weighs 3,200 g on day 3. The weight loss is about:
General.w: (3,500 - 3,200) ÷ 3,500 × 100 = 8.6%, within the acceptable 10%; 12% would need feeding assessment.

General.q: A baby has heart rate over 100, slow irregular breathing, some flexion, grimace and a blue colour. The APGAR score is:
General.w: Heart rate over 100 = 2, slow breathing = 1, some flexion = 1, grimace = 1, blue colour = 0, so 2 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 0 = 5 (moderately depressed); 4 or 6 come from mis-scoring one sign.

General.q: A woman has pulse 110 and systolic BP 100 mmHg. Her shock index is:
General.w: SI = 110 ÷ 100 = 1.1, above 1.0 and so a sign of major haemorrhage. 0.9 would need a pulse of 90 at the same BP; 0.5 is normal.

General.q: The commonest cause of PPH is:
General.w: Tone (uterine atony) causes about 70% of PPH, so massage and a uterotonic are the first actions; trauma 20%, tissue 10%, thrombin 1%.

General.q: The mean arterial pressure at 160/110 mmHg is:
General.w: MAP = (160 + 2 × 110) ÷ 3 = 126.7. Using 110 or 160 alone ignores that the diastolic pressure counts twice.

General.q: A fasting glucose of 5.1 mmol/L is in mg/dL:
General.w: 5.1 × 18 = 91.8, about 92 mg/dL, the WHO fasting cut-off for GDM. 180 mg/dL is the 1-hour value.

General.q: A baby's bilirubin is 20 mg/dL. In μmol/L this is about:
General.w: 20 × 17.1 = 342 μmol/L, a level at which exchange transfusion may be considered by the chart. 117 μmol/L is 6.8 mg/dL.

Office Management and Procedure.q: Write any two areas of office management.
Office Management and Procedure.r: Any two of: personnel; layout and environment; machines and equipment; records management; forms and stationery; communication; financial office work.

Office Management and Procedure.q: Name any two office procedures related to decision making.
Office Management and Procedure.r: Any two of: receipt and sorting, recording, action, noting and drafting, approval and signature, dispatch, follow-up.

Office Management and Procedure.q: What is meant by the retention period of a record?
Office Management and Procedure.r: The retention period is the fixed length of time for which a class of record must be kept before it may be transferred or destroyed.

Office Management and Procedure.q: Explain any five importance of office management in a business organisation.
Office Management and Procedure.r: (i) Speed of work — a laid-out office with a written procedure clears a file quickly. (ii) Accuracy of records — systematic recording answers any question about a past transaction. (iii) Coordination — every department works from the same information. (iv) Cost control — right stationery, furniture and staffing keep the cost per transaction low. (v) Goodwill — prompt, accurate replies win the confidence of customers and citizens. (Also: decision making, legal protection.)

Office Management and Procedure.q: What is office layout? Explain the open and the closed layout, giving two advantages and two disadvantages of each.
Office Management and Procedure.r: Layout is the arrangement of furniture, machines, departments and staff in the available space so that work flows smoothly. Open: advantages — cheap, easy supervision, quick paper movement; disadvantages — noise, no privacy, distraction. Closed: advantages — privacy and quiet, confidential work protected, status; disadvantages — high rent and furniture cost, weak supervision, longer paper travel, more lighting.

Office Management and Procedure.q: What is filing? Explain any five essential features of a good filing system.
Office Management and Procedure.r: Filing is the systematic arrangement and storage of documents so that any document can be traced and produced when needed. Features: simplicity; prompt location; economy; flexibility; safety; accessibility; compactness; cross-reference. (Any five explained.)

Office Management and Procedure.q: Write the full form of the register in which a government office enters every paper handled during the day.
Office Management and Procedure.r: The toc register (the day-book of papers handled).

Office Management and Procedure.q: Write any two points to be remembered while drafting a letter.
Office Management and Procedure.r: Any two of: state the purpose in the first two lines, one subject only, seven parts present, clear and courteous language, check every figure against the file.

Office Management and Procedure.q: What is office layout? Explain any four principles to be followed while arranging an office.
Office Management and Procedure.r: Layout is the arrangement of furniture, machines, departments and people in the available space. Principles: (i) straight-line flow — work moves forward, never backward; (ii) minimum movement — sections that exchange papers sit near each other; (iii) light and ventilation — light from the left of a right-handed worker, cross-ventilation; (iv) flexibility — movable furniture and partitions. (Also: space for movement, supervision, safety and cleanliness.)

Office Management and Procedure.q: Compare the open and the closed office layout, giving two advantages and two disadvantages of each.
Office Management and Procedure.r: Open: advantages — cheap, easy supervision, quick paper movement; disadvantages — noise, no privacy, distraction. Closed: advantages — privacy and quiet, confidential work protected, status; disadvantages — high rent and furniture cost, weak supervision, longer paper travel, more lighting.

Office Management and Procedure.q: Mention the aspects to be considered while preparing a report.
Office Management and Procedure.r: (i) Clear terms of reference stated at the beginning. (ii) Method of collecting information. (iii) Facts with dates and figures before opinion. (iv) Proper structure — title, terms of reference, method, findings, analysis, conclusion, recommendations. (v) Objectivity, practical and specific recommendations, brevity, and confidentiality where required.

Office Management and Procedure.q: Explain the objectives of indexing and describe any four types of index.
Office Management and Procedure.r: Objectives of indexing: to trace a file in the shortest time, to prevent loss, to enable cross-reference, to make numerical filing workable, to save the time of senior staff. Types: page, card, slip, visible, strip, wheel, loose-leaf and computer index. (Any four described.)

Office Management and Procedure.q: What is an office procedure? Explain the stages of an office procedure and state the principles of a good procedure.
Office Management and Procedure.r: Definition (2). An office procedure is the fixed sequence of steps by which a particular item of office work is completed and which tells every clerk what happens next, who signs and where the paper goes. Stages (4). (i) Receipt — paper arrives and is entered in the inward register. (ii) Sorting — urgent separated from routine, each item routed to the right section. (iii) Recording — number, date and file reference given. (iv) Action — the concerned section does the work. (v) Noting and drafting — facts recorded and the outgoing letter prepared. (vi) Approval and signature — the authorised officer approves and the fair copy is signed.

Office Management and Procedure.q: Explain the different methods and classifications of filing, and discuss the advantages and disadvantages of centralised filing against decentralised filing.
Office Management and Procedure.r: Methods (3). Horizontal (files lie flat, suits loose papers); vertical (files stand upright with the title on a visible tab — the commonest and fastest); lateral (upright with the tabs facing sideways, saves floor space); suspension (files hang from rails so they cannot fall). Classifications (3). Alphabetical by name; numerical; alphanumerical; chronological by date; subject or functional; geographical; decimal; colour coded. Each should be described with its main advantage and limit. Centralised vs decentralised (2).

Office Management and Procedure.q: What is records management? Explain the stages in the life of a record and the method of disposing of records that are no longer needed.
Office Management and Procedure.r: Definition (1). Records management is the policy and practice that decides how long each class of record is kept, where it is kept, and how it is disposed of. Life of a record (4). Current — in daily use, kept in the section. Semi-current — used occasionally, transferred to the record room. Non-current — no longer used, awaiting disposal. The retention period of each class is fixed by law, audit requirement and administrative need (cash books and ledgers permanently; vouchers five to ten years; personnel files until three years after exit; routine correspondence two to five years; title documents permanently). Methods of disposal (2). Retention;

Office Management and Procedure.q: What is office management? Explain its importance in eight points.
Define filing. Explain the types and methods of filing, with their advantages.
What does the term 'workflow' specifically refer to in an office environment?
o: The physical arrangement of office equipment
The sequence of steps in processing tasks or information
The budget allocated for office supplies
The number of employees in the office
Office Management and Procedure.w: Workflow in an office context refers to the process flow and task sequences.

Office Management and Procedure.q: Which system in office management ensures that all employees have access to necessary information when needed?
Office Management and Procedure.w: An Information System facilitates the flow of information within an organization.

Office Management and Procedure.q: In office management, what is the primary purpose of establishing a document control system?
o: To manage the creation, review, approval, and distribution of documents
To ensure the cleanliness and maintenance of office premises
To monitor the attendance of employees
To handle customer complaints and feedback
Office Management and Procedure.w: Document control systems manage the lifecycle of documents to maintain accuracy and availability.

Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutio.q: When was Nepal Rastra Bank established?
Write any two functions of a central bank.
Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutio.r: Any two of: issuing currency; banker to the government; banker's bank; lender of last resort; monetary policy; foreign exchange management; supervision of banks; clearing house.

Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutio.q: Name the first bank of Nepal with the year of its establishment.
Write any two kinds of non-life insurance.
Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutio.r: Any two of: fire, marine, motor, health, accident, crop and livestock insurance.

Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutio.q: What is meant by crossing a cheque?
Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutio.r: Crossing means drawing two parallel lines across the face of a cheque, directing the bank to pay it only into a bank account and never in cash.

Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutio.q: Distinguish between the money market and the capital market in one line.
Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutio.r: The money market deals in short-term funds and securities of up to one year; the capital market deals in long-term securities of more than one year.

Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutio.q: What is a central bank? Explain any five functions of a central bank.
Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutio.r: A central bank is the apex financial institution, dealing with the government and the banks rather than the public; Nepal Rastra Bank, 26 April 1956 A.D. (2013 B.S.). Five functions: currency issue; banker to the government; banker's bank and clearing house; lender of last resort; monetary policy. (Also foreign exchange management, supervision of banks, promotion of the financial sector.)

Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutio.q: What is insurance? Explain the principle on which it works and describe any three kinds of insurance.
Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutio.r: Insurance is a contract in which the insurer, in return for a premium, pays the insured on the happening of a stated event. Principle: pooling of risk — many pay a small premium into one fund from which the few who suffer a loss are paid, so the loss of one is spread over the group; the three conditions are many similar exposures, a loss measurable in money, and an insurable interest. Kinds: life (whole-life, endowment, money-back, term); fire; marine; motor; health; accident; crop and livestock. (Any three described.)

Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutio.q: Name the first bank of Nepal and the year it was established.
Explain any five functions of a commercial bank.
Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutio.r: (i) Accepting deposits — savings, current (cheque account), fixed and recurring. (ii) Advancing loans — cash credit, overdraft, demand loan, term loan, bill discounting. (iii) Credit creation. (iv) Agency services — collecting cheques and bills, paying bills and premiums, buying and selling securities, safe custody. (v) General utility services — drafts, pay orders, cards, mobile and internet banking, remittance and foreign exchange business.

Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutio.q: Distinguish between banking and non-banking financial institutions with suitable examples.
Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutio.r: Banking institutions accept demand deposits, operate cheque accounts and create credit: central bank, commercial banks, development banks, finance companies, microfinance institutions. Non-banking institutions collect public money and render financial services but do not accept demand deposits and cannot create credit: insurance companies, Employees' Provident Fund, Citizen Investment Trust, mutual funds and financial cooperatives. Give one example of each.

Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutio.q: What is insurance? Explain the principle on which insurance works and describe any three kinds of insurance.
Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutio.r: Insurance is a contract under which the insurer pays the insured on the happening of a stated event in return for a premium. It works on the pooling of risk: many pay a small premium into one fund from which the few who suffer a loss are paid, so the loss of an individual is spread over the group. Conditions: many similar exposures, a loss capable of being estimated in money, and an insurable interest. Any three kinds: life (whole life, endowment, money-back, term), fire, marine, motor, health, accident, crop or livestock insurance.

Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutio.q: Describe any five banking instruments used in Nepal.
Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutio.r: Cheque (open, order or crossed — a written order on the bank; only against a current account); bank draft (the bank's own order to pay, used where the payer has no account); pay order (the bank undertakes to pay a fixed amount to a named person, used for taxes and tenders); letter of credit (the bank promises to pay the exporter against shipping documents); debit and credit cards (access to one's own account; a short-term borrowing limit); mobile and internet banking (payment instructions from a phone or a website, used for bills and transfers). (Any five, each explained.)

Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutio.q: What is remittance? Explain its importance for the economy of Nepal.
Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutio.r: Remittance is money sent by a person working away from home, usually abroad, to a person at home. For Nepal it matters because (i) it is one of the largest single sources of foreign exchange; (ii) it sustains household consumption, education, health and house construction; (iii) it reduces pressure on the balance of payments because it does not have to be repaid; (iv) it creates the savings that bank deposits and cooperatives are built from; (v) it employs a large number of people in the transfer business. Its risks are dependence on foreign labour markets and the loss to hundi, the illegal informal channel.

Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutio.q: What is a bank? Explain the primary functions of a commercial bank and show, with a suitable example, how a commercial bank creates credit.
Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutio.r: Definition (2). A bank is a financial institution that accepts deposits from the public, lends money and provides payment services, aiming at profit. Primary functions (4). (i) Accepting deposits — savings, current, fixed, recurring; only the current account carries a cheque. (ii) Advancing loans — cash credit, overdraft, demand loan, term loan, bill discounting, hire purchase. (iii) Credit creation. (Also agency and general utility functions may be given briefly.) Credit creation (2). Suppose a bank receives a deposit of Rs. 10,000 and the cash reserve ratio is 10 per cent. It keeps Rs. 1,000 and lends Rs. 9,000. The borrower spends it, the receiver deposits it in a bank, which keeps Rs.

Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutio.q: What is insurance? Explain the principle of insurance and compare life insurance with non-life insurance.
Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutio.r: Definition (1). Insurance is a contract in which the insurer, in return for a premium, agrees to pay a stated sum to the insured on the happening of a stated event. Principle (3). Pooling of risk — many persons exposed to a similar risk each contribute a small premium to a common fund, and the few who actually suffer a loss are compensated from that fund, so the loss of one is shared by all. Three conditions are needed: a large number of similar exposures, a loss that can be measured in money, and an insurable interest. Comparison (4).

Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutio.q: Define a commercial bank. Explain its functions in eight points.
Explain the functions of the central bank of Nepal and distinguish it from a commercial bank.
Which of the following financial institutions primarily focuses on mobilizing savings from the public and channeling them into productive sectors?
Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutio.w: Commercial Banks play a pivotal role in collecting deposits from the public and lending to various sectors.

Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutio.q: What type of financial institution would you approach if you needed a long-term loan for your business expansion?
Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutio.w: Development Banks provide medium to long-term loans for business and industrial projects.

Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutio.q: Which of the following best describes the role of an insurance company in the economy?
Bank, Insurance and Financial Institutio.w: Insurance companies mitigate risks by pooling resources from policyholders and providing financial protection against losses.

Introduction to Tax.q: Write any two examples of direct tax.
Introduction to Tax.r: Any two of: income tax, house and land tax, capital gains tax, vehicle tax.

Introduction to Tax.q: Write the full form of VAT.
When was VAT introduced in Nepal?
What is the present rate of VAT in Nepal?
Write the full form of PAN and state how many digits it has.
Write any two sources of revenue of the Government of Nepal.
Introduction to Tax.r: Any two of: income tax, VAT, excise duty, customs duty, land and house tax, vehicle tax, registration fees, royalties, dividends from public enterprises, foreign grants.

Introduction to Tax.q: What is tax? Explain the principles of a good tax system.
Introduction to Tax.r: A tax is a compulsory contribution imposed by the government on persons, goods, services and transactions to meet public expenditure, without a direct and proportionate return. Principles: equality (ability to pay); certainty (the taxpayer knows how much, when and where to pay); convenience (collection suited to the taxpayer — VAT at the point of sale, income tax at source); economy (low collection cost). Add simplicity, flexibility and neutrality.

Introduction to Tax.q: Distinguish between direct tax and indirect tax with suitable examples.
Introduction to Tax.r: Direct: levied on income or property; borne by the person legally liable; cannot be shifted; collected directly; examples income tax, house and land tax, capital gains tax. Indirect: levied on goods, services and transactions; collected by the seller and paid over; the burden is shifted to the final consumer; raises the price; examples VAT, excise duty, customs duty. State that the test is who bears the burden, not who hands over the money.

Introduction to Tax.q: What is VAT? Explain how it is calculated by the input-credit method.
Introduction to Tax.r: VAT is an indirect tax on the value added at each stage of production and distribution; in Nepal from 1 Mangsir 2054 B.S., under the VAT Act 2052 and Rules 2053, at a single rate of 13 per cent. Method: every registered dealer charges tax on sales (output tax) and pays tax on purchases (input tax), and deposits output tax minus input tax. Because each dealer gets credit for the tax already paid by his supplier, no tax falls twice on the same value, and the total collected equals the VAT on the final price, borne by the consumer.

Introduction to Tax.q: Write any two sources of non-tax revenue.
Introduction to Tax.r: Any two of: fees and service charges, fines and penalties, registration fees, royalties, dividends from public enterprises, interest, rent, foreign grants.

Introduction to Tax.q: Write the full form of PAN.
How many digits are there in a PAN?
Which tax is called a progressive tax?
Introduction to Tax.r: A tax whose rate rises as the income or wealth of the taxpayer rises, so that the rich pay a larger share of their income than the poor.

Introduction to Tax.q: Explain any five objectives of taxation.
Introduction to Tax.r: (i) To raise revenue for public expenditure. (ii) To redistribute income and wealth between rich and poor. (iii) To control inflation by withdrawing purchasing power. (iv) To protect domestic industries through customs duty. (v) To discourage harmful consumption such as alcohol and tobacco. (Also: encourage saving and investment, promote balanced regional development.)

Introduction to Tax.q: What is meant by Permanent Account Number? Explain its importance and the persons who must obtain it.
Introduction to Tax.r: PAN is a unique nine-digit permanent number issued by the Inland Revenue Department to a taxpayer and valid for life. Importance: it identifies the taxpayer, enables tax deduction at source, is required in bank transactions and in bills and invoices, lets the tax office cross-check a taxpayer's transactions, and thus reduces evasion. It is compulsory for those carrying on industry, trade, business or profession, for employees and for anyone who must deduct tax at source; others may take it voluntarily. It is personal for an individual and business for a firm or company.

Introduction to Tax.q: What is revenue? Describe the sources of government revenue in Nepal.
Introduction to Tax.r: Revenue is the income raised by a government for public expenditure. Sources: tax revenue — direct taxes (income tax, house and land tax, capital gains tax, vehicle tax) and indirect taxes (VAT, excise duty, customs duty, entertainment tax); non-tax revenue — fees and service charges, fines and penalties, registration fees, royalties from mines and forests, dividends from public enterprises, interest on loans, rent of government property, and foreign grants and aid. Tax revenue provides more than 85 per cent of Nepal's total revenue.

Introduction to Tax.q: What is tax? Explain the classification of taxes with examples, and state the principles of a good tax system.
Introduction to Tax.r: Definition (1). A tax is a compulsory contribution imposed by the government on persons, goods, services and transactions to meet public expenditure, without a direct and proportionate return to the payer. Classification (4). (i) Direct tax — borne by the person on whom it is legally imposed and not shiftable: income tax, house and land tax, capital gains tax, vehicle tax. (ii) Indirect tax — imposed on one person but borne by another, shifted to the final consumer: VAT, excise duty, customs duty, entertainment tax. (iii) By effect on income — progressive, proportional, regressive, digressive. (iv) By base — tax on income, on capital, on expenditure, on property.

Introduction to Tax.q: A producer sells goods to a wholesaler for Rs. 2,00,000, the wholesaler sells to a retailer for Rs. 2,40,000 and the retailer sells to the consumer for Rs. 2,60,000, all prices being exclusive of VAT. The VAT rate is 13 per cent. Compute the VAT deposited by each dealer, the total VAT received by the government, and verify the total against the VAT on the final price.
Introduction to Tax.r: Producer: sale Rs. 2,00,000; output tax $= 13\% \times 2{,}00{,}000 = Rs.\ 26{,}000$; input tax nil; deposit Rs. 26,000. Wholesaler: sale Rs. 2,40,000; output tax $= 13\% \times 2{,}40{,}000 = Rs.\ 31{,}200$; input tax Rs. 26,000; deposit $= 31{,}200 - 26{,}000 =$ Rs. 5,200. Retailer: sale Rs. 2,60,000; output tax $= 13\% \times 2{,}60{,}000 = Rs.\ 33{,}800$; input tax Rs. 31,200; deposit $= 33{,}800 - 31{,}200 =$ Rs. 2,600. Total deposited $= 26{,}000 + 5{,}200 + 2{,}600 = Rs.\ 33{,}800$. Verification: $13\% \times 2{,}60{,}000 = Rs.\ 33{,}800$. Equal — the whole tax is ultimately borne by the consumer and collected in instalments along the chain.

Introduction to Tax.q: What is a tax? Explain direct and indirect taxes with examples and a comparison table.
What is Value Added Tax? Explain its features and show by an example how the VAT payable is found.

Business Accounting.q: Name any two types of accounting.
Business Accounting.r: Any two of: financial accounting, cost accounting, management accounting.

Business Accounting.q: Name the body that issues accounting standards in Nepal.
Business Accounting.r: The Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nepal (ICAN), through its Accounting Standards Board.

Business Accounting.q: Write the full form of NFRS.
Write any two external users of accounting information.
Business Accounting.r: Any two of: banks and lenders, suppliers and creditors, the government and the tax authority, investors, auditors, the public.

Business Accounting.q: Distinguish between book-keeping and accounting in one line.
Business Accounting.r: Book-keeping is only the recording of transactions in the journal and ledger; accounting goes further and includes summarising, analysing and interpreting the recorded data and preparing the final accounts.

Business Accounting.q: Why do business organisations use accounting? Explain any five reasons.
Business Accounting.r: To keep a systematic, evidence-based record of every transaction; to find the profit or loss of a period; to show the financial position on a date; to give the owner information for control and decision; to satisfy the tax office, the auditor and the courts; to attract investors and lenders.

Business Accounting.q: Who are the users of accounting information? Explain any five and state what each wants.
Business Accounting.r: Internal: owners/shareholders (profit and the value of their investment), management (cost, product-wise profit, cash position), employees (wages, bonus, job security). External: banks and lenders (ability to repay, security), suppliers and creditors (ability to pay in time), the government and tax authority (correct income tax and VAT), investors (earnings and risk), auditors (evidence), the public (fair price and continuity). (Any five, with what each wants.)

Business Accounting.q: What is a chart of accounts? Explain its structure and importance in an office.
Business Accounting.r: The chart of accounts is the numbered list of all account heads. Structure: five groups — assets (1), liabilities (2), capital (3), income (4), expenses (5) — then sub-groups and individual accounts, the code being hierarchical so the first digit names the group. Importance: one name and one code for every head, so different clerks record alike; easy sorting and totalling; makes computerised accounting possible; and in government a uniform chart of accounts lets the accounts of all offices be consolidated.

Business Accounting.q: Which asset is increased by a debit?
Business Accounting.r: An asset is increased by a debit (e.g. furniture, cash, stock).

Business Accounting.q: Why do business organisations use accounting? Give any two reasons.
Business Accounting.r: Any two of: to keep a systematic record, to find profit or loss, to show the financial position, to control the business, to satisfy the tax office and the auditor, to take decisions.

Business Accounting.q: Explain the objectives of financial accounting.
Business Accounting.r: Systematic record; ascertainment of profit or loss by matching income with the expenses of the same period; presentation of the financial position; supply of information for control; provision of evidence for tax, audit and legal purposes; communication of the result to the interested parties.

Business Accounting.q: Who are the users of accounting information? Explain any five of them and what each wants.
Business Accounting.r: Owners/shareholders want profit and the value of their investment; management wants cost, product-wise profit and the cash position for decisions; employees want wages, bonus and job security; banks and lenders want the ability to repay and the security available; suppliers and creditors want the ability to pay within the credit period; the government and tax authority want income tax and VAT correctly assessed; investors want earnings and risk; auditors want evidence for their report; the public wants a fair price and continuity of supply. (Any five with what each wants.)

Business Accounting.q: What is an accounting standard? Explain its importance and name any three standards used in Nepal.
Business Accounting.r: A standard is a written rule on recognition, measurement, presentation and disclosure. Importance: comparability between businesses, consistency from year to year, reliability so that a lender may trust a statement without visiting the business, and an objective yardstick for the auditor. Standards in Nepal: NFRS, NFRS for SMEs and NAS; examples NAS 2 (inventories), NAS 16 (property, plant and equipment), NAS 18 (revenue).

Business Accounting.q: Distinguish between book-keeping, accounting and accountancy.
Business Accounting.r: Book-keeping is only the recording stage — writing the journal, posting to the ledger, balancing the accounts; it is routine and clerical. Accounting goes further: it summarises, analyses and interprets the recorded data and prepares the final accounts.
