Accountancy is the whole body of knowledge, including the principles, standards and rules on which accounting is based. Book-keeping is a part of accounting, and accounting is a part of accountancy.

Business Accounting.q: What is accounting? Explain the steps of the accounting cycle and state the rules of debit and credit with the accounting equation.
Business Accounting.r: Definition (1). Accounting is the process of identifying, measuring, recording, classifying, summarising and communicating economic information so that users can take decisions. Accounting cycle (4). (i) Identify and measure the transaction in money. (ii) Record it in the journal with a narration and a voucher. (iii) Post to the ledger accounts. (iv) Balance the accounts and prepare the trial balance. (v) Make adjustments and rectify errors. (vi) Prepare the trading and profit and loss account and the balance sheet. (vii) Communicate the result to the users. Explain each step in one sentence and say that the cycle repeats every year. Equation and rules (3). $Assets = Liabilities + Capital$;

Business Accounting.q: What is an accounting standard? Explain the accounting standards in force in Nepal and their importance to a business and to a bank that is considering a loan.
Business Accounting.r: Definition (1). A written rule issued by an authorised professional body prescribing how transactions must be recognised, measured, presented and disclosed. Standards in Nepal (3). Issued by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nepal through its Accounting Standards Board: NFRS for listed companies and large public-interest entities; NFRS for SMEs for smaller entities; NAS for the rest. Give examples such as NAS 2 (inventories), NAS 16 (property, plant and equipment), NAS 18 (revenue) and NAS 7 (cash flows). Importance (4). Comparability — two businesses in the same trade can be compared; consistency — the same basis year after year;

Business Accounting.q: Define accounting. Explain the objectives and importance of financial accounting in eight points.
What are accounting standards? Explain the need for them and the Nepal Accounting Standards.

Bank Reconciliation Statement.q: What is a bank reconciliation statement?
Bank Reconciliation Statement.r: A statement prepared on a particular date to explain and reconcile the difference between the balance of the bank column of the cash book and the balance of the passbook.

Bank Reconciliation Statement.q: Write any two causes of the difference between the cash book and the passbook.
Bank Reconciliation Statement.r: Any two of: cheques issued but not presented; cheques deposited but not collected; bank charges; interest allowed or charged; direct deposit by a customer; standing instructions; dishonoured cheque; errors.

Bank Reconciliation Statement.q: What does a debit balance in the cash book (bank column) mean?
Bank Reconciliation Statement.r: Money is lying in the bank — a favourable balance.

Bank Reconciliation Statement.q: If the cash book shows an overdraft, what kind of balance does the passbook show?
Bank Reconciliation Statement.r: A debit balance (an overdraft in the cash book is a debit balance in the passbook).

Bank Reconciliation Statement.q: A cheque issued but not presented makes the passbook balance higher or lower than the cash book balance?
Bank Reconciliation Statement.r: Higher — the trader has already reduced his cash book, the bank has not.

Bank Reconciliation Statement.q: Write any two items recorded by the bank only.
Bank Reconciliation Statement.r: Any two of: bank charges and commission, interest allowed or charged, dividend collected, direct deposit by a customer, standing instructions, dishonour of a cheque.

Bank Reconciliation Statement.q: What is the adjusted cash book?
Bank Reconciliation Statement.r: The cash book after all items appearing only in the passbook have been entered in it, so that the remaining difference is only a matter of time.

Bank Reconciliation Statement.q: A cheque deposited is dishonoured. Which book shows it first?
Why is a bank reconciliation statement prepared? Give any one reason.
Bank Reconciliation Statement.r: To check the accuracy of both records and find errors; to find the true bank balance; to detect dishonoured cheques and unrecorded charges; to prepare the balance sheet; to prevent fraud.

Bank Reconciliation Statement.q: Name the statement prepared to bring the cash book and the passbook into agreement.
What is a bank reconciliation statement? Explain any four causes of the difference between the cash book and the passbook.
Bank Reconciliation Statement.r: Definition: a statement prepared on a date to explain and reconcile the difference between the bank column of the cash book and the passbook. Causes: cheques issued but not presented (cash book lower); cheques deposited but not collected (cash book higher); items recorded by the bank only — bank charges, interest, dividend collected, direct deposits, standing instructions, dishonoured cheques; and errors in either book.

Bank Reconciliation Statement.q: The cash book of a firm showed a bank balance of Rs. 65,000 on 30 Chaitra. Cheques issued but not presented Rs. 12,000; cheques deposited but not collected Rs. 8,000; bank charges Rs. 1,500; interest on investment collected by the bank Rs. 6,000; a customer deposited Rs. 9,000 directly into the bank. Prepare the bank reconciliation statement.
Explain the effect on the cash book and on the passbook of:
p: a direct deposit by a customer,
the dishonour of a cheque deposited.
Bank Reconciliation Statement.r: (a) Cheque issued — cash book decreases at once; the passbook is unaffected until the cheque is presented. (b) Cheque deposited — cash book increases at once; the passbook is unaffected until it is collected. (c) Bank charges — no effect on the cash book until known; the passbook decreases at once. (d) Direct deposit by a customer — no effect on the cash book until known; the passbook increases at once. (e) Dishonour of a cheque deposited — the passbook decreases when the bank returns it; the cash book must then be corrected.

Bank Reconciliation Statement.q: A cheque of Rs. 5,000 issued on 28 Chaitra is presented on 4 Baisakh. In which book is it recorded on 31 Chaitra?
Bank Reconciliation Statement.r: Only in the cash book; the bank will record it when the cheque is presented in Baisakh.

Bank Reconciliation Statement.q: Write any two items that are recorded by the bank only.
Bank Reconciliation Statement.r: Any two of: bank charges and commission, interest allowed or charged, dividend collected, direct deposit by a customer, standing instructions, dishonour of a cheque.

Bank Reconciliation Statement.q: A cheque deposited was dishonoured. Which book shows it first?
Bank Reconciliation Statement.r: The passbook shows it first; the trader learns of it afterwards.

Bank Reconciliation Statement.q: When cheques are issued but not presented, is the passbook balance higher or lower than the cash book balance?
Bank Reconciliation Statement.r: Higher — the trader has already reduced his cash book, the bank has not.

Bank Reconciliation Statement.q: The passbook of a trader showed a credit balance of Rs. 55,000 on 31 Ashad. Cheques issued but not presented Rs. 20,000; cheques deposited but not collected Rs. 9,000; bank charges Rs. 800; interest allowed by the bank Rs. 3,800. Prepare the bank reconciliation statement.
Explain the effect on the cash book and on the passbook of:
p: a direct deposit by a customer,
a dishonest dishonour of a cheque deposited.
Bank Reconciliation Statement.r: (a) Cheque issued — cash book decreases at once; the passbook is unaffected until the cheque is presented. (b) Cheque deposited — cash book increases at once; the passbook is unaffected until the cheque is collected. (c) Bank charges — no effect on the cash book until known; the passbook decreases at once. (d) Direct deposit by a customer — no effect on the cash book until known; the passbook increases at once. (e) Cheque deposited dishonoured — the passbook decreases when the bank returns it; the cash book must then be corrected. (Note: the phrase in the question is a typo for "dishonour".)

Bank Reconciliation Statement.q: Why is a bank reconciliation statement prepared? Explain any five reasons.
Bank Reconciliation Statement.r: (i) To check the accuracy of both records and to trace errors of the trader or of the bank. (ii) To find the real bank balance available for drawing and for the balance sheet. (iii) To detect dishonoured cheques, bank charges and direct deposits that the trader has missed. (iv) To prevent and detect fraud by a cashier. (v) Because it is required by the auditor and by the bank before granting further credit.

Bank Reconciliation Statement.q: What is a bank reconciliation statement? Explain its need and the causes which make the cash book and the passbook differ, and show the usual format starting from the cash book balance.
Bank Reconciliation Statement.r: Definition (1). As in Group A answer 1. Need (3). Accuracy check on both books; finding the true bank balance; detecting dishonoured cheques, missed charges and direct deposits; preparing the balance sheet; preventing fraud; satisfying the auditor and the bank. Causes (2). Timing: cheques issued but not presented, cheques deposited but not collected. Bank-only entries: bank charges and commission, interest allowed or charged, dividend or interest collected, direct deposits, standing instructions, dishonoured cheques. Errors: in the cash book or in the passbook. Format (2). Start with the cash book balance;

Bank Reconciliation Statement.q: The cash book (bank column) of a trader shows a debit balance of Rs 48,000 on 31 Ashad. Cheques issued but not presented Rs 9,000; cheques deposited but not collected Rs 6,000; bank charges Rs 400 and interest collected by the bank on an investment Rs 2,400 (both only in the passbook); a customer paid Rs 5,000 directly into the bank; the bank paid an insurance premium Rs 1,500 under a standing instruction. Prepare the bank reconciliation statement and the adjusted cash book.
Explain the causes of the difference between the cash book and the passbook, and the effect of each on the two books.
What is the purpose of preparing a bank reconciliation statement?
o: To reconcile the company's cash book with the bank statement
To ensure that all transactions are recorded in the sales ledger
To calculate the total revenue of the company
To adjust the bank statement to match the petty cash record
Bank Reconciliation Statement.w: The bank reconciliation statement aims to ensure consistency between the company's records and the bank's records.

Bank Reconciliation Statement.q: Which of the following would be subtracted from the bank statement balance while preparing a bank reconciliation statement?
Bank Reconciliation Statement.w: Bank service charges are usually debited by the bank but not yet recorded in the company's books, thus they need to be subtracted.

Bank Reconciliation Statement.q: If the bank has incorrectly charged an amount for a check that was never presented for payment, what action should be taken during bank reconciliation?
o: Add the amount to the bank statement balance
Subtract the amount from the bank statement balance
Record it as an expense in the company's books
Bank Reconciliation Statement.w: An incorrect charge by the bank means adding the amount back to the bank statement balance to correct it.

Bank Reconciliation Statement.q: During the preparation of a bank reconciliation statement, outstanding checks refer to which of the following?
o: Checks written by the company but not yet cleared by the bank
Checks received by the company but not yet deposited
Checks that were voided before being issued
Checks that were issued and cleared in the same period
Bank Reconciliation Statement.w: Outstanding checks are those checks issued by the company that have not yet been presented to the bank.

Accounting Errors.q: What is an error of principle? Give one example.
Accounting Errors.r: A mistake in applying an accounting rule, such as treating a capital expenditure as a revenue expense. Example: wages paid for installing a machine debited to the wages account instead of being added to the machine's cost.

Accounting Errors.q: Which errors are detected by the trial balance?
Accounting Errors.r: One-sided errors: casting and balancing errors, posting to the wrong side, a wrong amount posted in one account only, partial omission.

Accounting Errors.q: Which errors are not detected by the trial balance?
Accounting Errors.r: Two-sided errors: errors of principle, complete omission, compensating errors, wrong account of the same class, a transaction entered twice in both accounts.

Accounting Errors.q: If the debit column of the trial balance is short, on which side is the suspense account opened?
A purchase of machinery was debited to the purchases account. What kind of error is this?
What are accounting errors? Explain any five causes of accounting errors.
Accounting Errors.r: An accounting error is a mistake in recording, posting, casting, carrying forward or summarising a transaction or in applying an accounting principle. Causes: carelessness; ignorance of principle; wrong classification; wrong side; omission (complete or partial); compensating mistakes; faulty arithmetic; the wrong account of the same class.

Accounting Errors.q: Which errors are detected by the trial balance and which are not? Explain with examples.
Accounting Errors.r: Detected — one-sided errors: casting and balancing errors, posting to the wrong side, a wrong amount posted in one account only, partial omission; these change one side of the trial balance. Not detected — two-sided errors: errors of principle, complete omission, compensating errors, the wrong account of the same class, a transaction entered twice in both accounts; these leave the trial balance in agreement while the books are still wrong.

Accounting Errors.q: Write any two causes of accounting errors.
Accounting Errors.r: Any two of: carelessness, ignorance of accounting principle, wrong classification, posting to the wrong side, omission, compensating mistake, faulty arithmetic.

Accounting Errors.q: A sale of Rs. 5,000 to Ram was debited to Shyam. Will the trial balance agree?
Accounting Errors.r: Yes — both are debtors, so the total of the debit column is unchanged.

Accounting Errors.q: Explain the types of accounting errors with suitable examples.
Accounting Errors.r: Error of principle — treating capital expenditure as revenue (wages for installing machinery debited to wages). Error of omission — complete omission (a sale not entered anywhere) or partial omission (entered in the journal but not posted). Error of commission — wrong amount, wrong account, wrong side, wrong casting, wrong balance carried forward. Compensating error — wages overcast by Rs. 1,000 and sales undercast by Rs. 1,000.

Accounting Errors.q: The following errors were located after the preparation of the trial balance.
p: Salary paid Rs. 20,000 was wrongly debited to the house rent account.
The sales book was overcast by Rs. 5,000.
A purchase of furniture of Rs. 30,000 was debited to the purchases account.
A sale of Rs. 7,000 to Bina was posted to Bina's account as Rs. 700. Pass the rectifying entries and prepare the suspense account.
Accounting Errors.r: (a) Salary A/c Dr. 20,000; To House Rent A/c 20,000. Two-sided — the trial balance agreed, no suspense needed. (b) The sales book was overcast by Rs. 5,000: the credit side is too high, so the trial balance was short on the debit side and the suspense account was credited. Sales A/c Dr. 5,000; To Suspense A/c 5,000. (c) Furniture A/c Dr. 30,000; To Purchases A/c 30,000. Error of principle — two-sided, no suspense. (d) Bina's account was debited Rs. 700 instead of Rs. 7,000 — the debit side is short by Rs. 6,300. Bina A/c Dr. 6,300; To Suspense A/c 6,300.

Accounting Errors.q: What is an accounting error? Explain the types of errors, with an example of each, and say which of them the trial balance does not disclose.

The trial balance of a firm did not agree: the credit side exceeded the debit side by Rs 700 and the difference was put in a suspense account. Later these errors were found: (i) the sales returns book was undercast by Rs 1,000; (ii) rent of Rs 600 paid was debited to the rent account as Rs 900; (iii) goods bought from Hari for Rs 2,000 were debited to the furniture account. Pass the journal entries and prepare the suspense account.
A transaction of Rs. 300 was incorrectly debited to Rent Expense instead of Depreciation Expense. How should this be corrected?
o: Debit Rent Expense and credit Depreciation Expense by Rs. 600
Credit Rent Expense and debit Depreciation Expense by Rs. 300
Debit Rent Expense and credit Cash by Rs. 300
Credit Rent Expense and debit Bank by Rs. 300
Accounting Errors.w: The correction involves transferring the amount from Rent Expense to Depreciation Expense by reversing the incorrect entry.

Final Account.q: Write the formula for the cost of goods sold.
Final Account.r: $Cost\ of\ goods\ sold = Opening\ stock + Purchases + Direct\ expenses - Closing\ stock$.

Final Account.q: How is outstanding salary treated in the final accounts?
Final Account.r: Added to the salary on the debit side of the profit and loss account and shown as a current liability in the balance sheet.

Final Account.q: What is the treatment of prepaid rent?
Final Account.r: Deducted from rent on the debit side of the profit and loss account and shown as a current asset in the balance sheet.

Final Account.q: Where does the closing stock appear?
Final Account.r: Credited in the trading account on the credit side and shown as a current asset in the balance sheet.

Final Account.q: How are drawings treated in the balance sheet?
Final Account.r: Deducted from the capital on the liabilities side.

Final Account.q: What is a provision for doubtful debts?
Final Account.r: An amount set aside out of profit to cover debts expected not to be recovered; it is debited to the profit and loss account and deducted from debtors.

Final Account.q: What are final accounts? Explain their objectives.
Final Account.r: Final accounts are the statements prepared at the end of the accounting period from the trial balance after adjustments, to show the profit or loss of the period and the financial position on the closing date. Objectives: to find the gross profit or loss; to find the net profit or loss; to show the financial position; to make comparison possible; to provide the basis for tax and audit; to help the owner decide. (Any five explained.)

Final Account.q: Explain the effect of any five adjustments on the trading account, the profit and loss account and the balance sheet.

From the following, compute the gross profit and the net profit. Opening stock Rs. 25,000; purchases Rs. 1,50,000; carriage inward Rs. 5,000; purchases returns Rs. 5,000; wages Rs. 20,000; sales Rs. 2,20,000; sales returns Rs. 10,000; closing stock Rs. 35,000; salary Rs. 18,000; rent Rs. 12,000; discount received Rs. 4,000.
Write any two objectives of preparing final accounts.
Final Account.r: Any two of: to find the gross profit, to find the net profit, to show the financial position, to allow comparison with past years, to provide the basis for tax and audit, to help the owner decide.

Final Account.q: Explain the components of the financial statements prepared by a trading concern.
Final Account.r: The trading account shows the gross result of buying and selling: opening stock, purchases, direct expenses and gross profit on the debit side; sales and closing stock on the credit side. The profit and loss account shows the net result: the gross profit and other income on the credit side; indirect expenses such as office salary, rent, depreciation and interest on the debit side. The balance sheet is a statement of assets, liabilities and capital on the closing date, with the net profit added to capital and drawings deducted. Explain each with one example of an item that belongs in it.

Final Account.q: Why are accounting notes prepared with the financial statements? Explain any five points disclosed in them.
Final Account.r: Notes are prepared because the statements alone do not tell a reader which policies were applied, what a composite figure contains, or what obligations exist that do not appear as liabilities. They state the accounting policies (valuation of stock, method of depreciation); break down large items such as other expenses, debtors and creditors; give schedules of fixed assets, loans and investments; disclose contingent liabilities such as a pending court case or a guarantee given for another firm; disclose events after the balance sheet date; and reconcile the figures in the statements with the accounts.

Final Account.q: What are final accounts? Explain the steps in their preparation and the treatment of any five adjustments.
Final Account.r: Definition (1). As in Group A answer 1. Steps (3). Complete and agree the trial balance; bring in the closing entries for the trading account; prepare the trading account and find the gross profit; prepare the profit and loss account applying every remaining adjustment and find the net profit; add the net profit to capital and deduct drawings; prepare the balance sheet with the adjusted asset values and every outstanding, prepaid and accrued item; check that the two sides agree. Adjustments (4).

Final Account.q: The following is the trial balance of Himal Traders on 31 Chaitra 2082.
Final Account.r: Trading account for the year ended 31 Chaitra 2082

Final Account.q: What are final accounts? Explain their components and objectives, and the adjustments made at the year end.

From the following balances of a trader as on 31 Ashad prepare the trading account, the profit and loss account and the balance sheet. Opening stock 20,000; purchases 1,20,000; purchases returns 4,000; sales 2,10,000; sales returns 10,000; carriage inwards 3,000; wages 12,000; rent 6,000; salaries 24,000; office expenses 5,000; building 76,000; furniture 40,000; debtors 35,000; creditors 25,000; cash and bank 30,000; capital 1,50,000; drawings 8,000. Adjustments: closing stock 30,000; salaries outstanding 2,000; depreciation on furniture 4,000.
What is the term used to describe the financial statement that summarizes the revenues, expenses, and profits of a business over an accounting period?
Final Account.w: The Income Statement specifically shows the revenues, expenses, and profits over a specific period.

Final Account.q: In the context of final accounts, what does the term 'Closing Stock' refer to?
o: Stock at the beginning of the financial year
Cash in hand at the end of the financial year
Stock available at the end of the financial year
Final Account.w: Closing Stock is the inventory value at the end of an accounting period.

Final Account.q: Which of the following best describes the purpose of the Trading Account in final accounts?
o: To calculate gross profit or loss
To summarize cash inflows and outflows
Final Account.w: The Trading Account is primarily used to determine the gross profit or loss before deducting administrative and selling expenses.

System of Government Accounting in Nepal.q: Write any two bases of government accounting in Nepal.
System of Government Accounting in Nepal.r: Any two of: legal basis; cash basis; double-entry system; fund basis; uniformity of forms and chart of accounts; budget classification; two levels of accounting; banking arrangement; external audit.

System of Government Accounting in Nepal.q: Which basis of accounting does the Government of Nepal follow?
Which office manages government accounting in Nepal?
System of Government Accounting in Nepal.r: The Financial Comptroller General Office (महालेखा नियन्त्रक कार्यालय).

System of Government Accounting in Nepal.q: Write any two government offices that use central level accounting.
System of Government Accounting in Nepal.r: Any two of: the Ministry of Finance, the Office of the Auditor General, a ministry or department at the centre, the Financial Comptroller General Office.

System of Government Accounting in Nepal.q: What is operating level accounting?
System of Government Accounting in Nepal.r: The accounting of the transactions of a district or local office, kept in the office itself in the bank cash book and reported monthly through the statement of expenditure.

System of Government Accounting in Nepal.q: Write any two areas of government accounting.
System of Government Accounting in Nepal.r: Any two of: revenue accounting, expenditure accounting, store accounting, fund accounting, deposit and retention accounting, loan and grant accounting, asset and liability accounting.

System of Government Accounting in Nepal.q: Name the apex auditing body that audits government accounts in Nepal.
System of Government Accounting in Nepal.r: The Office of the Auditor General.

System of Government Accounting in Nepal.q: What is government accounting? Explain any five bases of government accounting in Nepal.
System of Government Accounting in Nepal.r: Government accounting is the system by which a government records, classifies, summarises and reports its revenue, expenditure and financial position for accountability to the legislature and the public. Bases: legal basis (Financial Procedures and Fiscal Responsibility Act 2076 and Rules 2077); cash basis; double-entry system; fund basis; uniformity of forms and chart of accounts. (Also budget classification, two levels of accounting, banking arrangement, external audit.)

System of Government Accounting in Nepal.q: Explain any five differences between commercial accounting and government accounting.
System of Government Accounting in Nepal.r: Objective — profit against accountability; basis — accrual against cash; ownership — private owners against the public; the budget — a plan against a law; funds — one general fund against several prescribed funds; statements — trading, profit and loss account and balance sheet against statements of revenue, expenditure and financial position; performance — profit against economy, efficiency and compliance; audit — a private auditor against the Office of the Auditor General.

System of Government Accounting in Nepal.q: What is a consolidated fund? Explain the provisions for its operation.
System of Government Accounting in Nepal.r: The consolidated fund is the government's main account: all revenue is paid into it and nothing may be withdrawn except under an appropriation made by law. Provisions: all government receipts credited to it; no payment without an appropriation act; use only for the approved purpose; unforeseen expenditure from the contingency fund, later regularised; managed by the Ministry of Finance and accounted for by the FCGO, the money kept with Nepal Rastra Bank; reported to the legislature and audited by the Auditor General; drawn only by the authorised officer within the release.

System of Government Accounting in Nepal.q: Write any two differences between commercial and government accounting.
System of Government Accounting in Nepal.r: Any two of: objective (profit against accountability); basis (accrual against cash); budget (plan against law); ownership (private owners against the public); audit (private auditor against the Auditor General).

System of Government Accounting in Nepal.q: Explain the accounting of the federal, provincial and local levels in Nepal.
System of Government Accounting in Nepal.r: The federation keeps its accounts through the ministries, departments and the FCGO; its revenue goes into the federal consolidated fund and its expenditure is met under the federal appropriation act. The provinces keep their accounts through the provincial ministries and the Provincial Treasury and Comptroller Offices; provincial revenue and the divisible fund money go into the provincial consolidated fund. The local levels (municipalities, rural municipalities, wards) keep their accounts through the Local Treasury and Comptroller Offices; their own taxes, fees and grants go into the local consolidated fund and the local assembly appropriates the expenditure.

System of Government Accounting in Nepal.q: What is the chart of accounts? Explain its structure and importance in government accounting.
System of Government Accounting in Nepal.r: The chart of accounts is the uniform coded list of all revenue heads, expenditure heads, funds and assets. Its structure follows the budget classification: first the organisational classification (ministry, office) and then the economic classification (remuneration 21111, allowance 21112, office materials 21121, uniform 22111, travelling expenses 22311, machinery 31111, furniture 31121). Importance: payments can be checked against the balance in the head before they are made; the auditor sees at once whether the right head was used; and because the codes are the same everywhere, the accounts of all offices can be consolidated into the national statement.

System of Government Accounting in Nepal.q: Distinguish between central level accounting and operating level accounting.
System of Government Accounting in Nepal.r: Central level accounting records transactions of the centre — payments made at the ministry or department, or expenditure booked centrally for the whole country — and is kept at the Financial Comptroller General Office and the central Treasury and Comptroller Office. Operating level accounting records the transactions of a district or local office — a salary paid, an advance issued, stationery bought — in the office itself, using the bank cash book and the prescribed vouchers, and is reported monthly to the Treasury and Comptroller Office through the statement of expenditure. The central level figures enter the general ledger directly;

System of Government Accounting in Nepal.q: What is government accounting? Explain the main bases of government accounting in Nepal and the differences between commercial and government accounting.
System of Government Accounting in Nepal.r: Definition (1). As in Group A answer 1. Bases (4). Legal basis, cash basis, double-entry system, fund basis, uniformity of forms and chart of accounts, budget classification, two levels of accounting, banking arrangement, external audit — explain any five or six in a sentence each. Differences (3). Objective, basis, ownership, standing of the budget, funds, statements prepared, performance measurement, audit. Give them as a table with a short explanation of each row.

System of Government Accounting in Nepal.q: What is the consolidated fund? Explain the provisions for its operation and distinguish it from the single account fund.
System of Government Accounting in Nepal.r: Consolidated fund (2). The government's main account: all revenue is deposited into it and nothing may be withdrawn from it except under an appropriation made by law. Provisions for its operation (3). All government receipts credited to it; expenditure only under an appropriation act; use only for the approved purposes; emergency expenditure from the contingency fund, later regularised; managed by the Ministry of Finance and accounted by the FCGO; payment only by the officer authorised to draw. Difference from the single account fund (3). The consolidated fund is about authority and ownership — it is the government's main fund and its use is controlled by the legislature.

System of Government Accounting in Nepal.q: What is government accounting? Explain the main bases of government accounting in Nepal and distinguish it from commercial accounting.
Explain the consolidated fund and the single account fund, and the levels of government accounting in Nepal.
What is the term used to describe the system where financial transactions of the government are recorded, classified, and summarized?
System of Government Accounting in Nepal.w: Government Accounting refers to the systematic recording of all financial transactions conducted by the government.

System of Government Accounting in Nepal.q: In the context of Nepalese Government Accounting, what does the term 'Fund' refer to?
o: A specific amount of money allocated for general purposes
A separate accounting entity with its own assets, liabilities, and budget
An investment portfolio managed by the government
System of Government Accounting in Nepal.w: In Nepalese Government Accounting, a fund represents a separate accounting entity with its own set of financial resources and obligations.

Revenue Accounting.q: Why must revenue be deposited into the bank on the same day?
Revenue Accounting.r: Because revenue must reach the consolidated fund and be accounted for, and an office that held it as cash could spend it outside the budget.

Revenue Accounting.q: Write the code for examination fee.
Write any two examples of non-tax revenue with codes.
Revenue Accounting.r: Any two of: 14227 passport fee; 14251 company registration fee; 14151 rent of government property; 14221 judicial fee; 14311 judicial fine.

Revenue Accounting.q: What is a revenue voucher (आम्दानी भौचर)?
Revenue Accounting.r: The voucher by which revenue is recorded in the accounts, naming the head, the payer, the amount and the evidence.

Revenue Accounting.q: Write the formula for checking a revenue statement.
Revenue Accounting.r: Revenue collected = amount deposited into the consolidated fund + cash still in hand.

Revenue Accounting.q: Write any two objectives of revenue accounting.
Revenue Accounting.r: Any two of: to record every rupee with evidence; to ensure deposit into the consolidated fund; to compare collection with the estimate; to detect leakage; to supply the government's financial statement; to keep the account public.

Revenue Accounting.q: What is revenue accounting? Explain its objectives.
Revenue Accounting.r: Revenue accounting records the collection of government revenue, its deposit into the consolidated fund through the bank and its reporting. Objectives: to record every rupee with evidence; to deposit the whole collection into the consolidated fund; to compare collection head by head with the estimate; to detect leakage; to supply the government's annual financial statement and the audit; to keep the revenue account public.

Revenue Accounting.q: Explain the banking arrangement of revenue accounting in Nepal.
Revenue Accounting.r: Each office has one designated bank account under the single account fund; all revenue is deposited into the consolidated fund through Nepal Rastra Bank or a commercial bank; the deposit is made the same day as the collection, or on the first working day with the reason recorded; the office may not pay any expense out of its collection; the bank reconciliation is prepared monthly; and the Treasury and Comptroller Office watches every office's deposits against its reported collection.

Revenue Accounting.q: A District Health Office collected the following revenue in the month of Falgun: 14151 rent of government property Rs. 2,38,800; 14213 other sales Rs. 41,000; 14224 examination fee Rs. 1,75,500 of which Rs. 35,100 was not deposited. Prepare the revenue statement.
Write any two examples of non-tax revenue with their codes.
Revenue Accounting.r: Any two of: 14227 passport fee, 14251 company registration fee, 14151 rent of government property, 14221 judicial fee, 14311 judicial fine.

Revenue Accounting.q: Where is the revenue of a government office deposited?
Revenue Accounting.r: Into the consolidated fund, through the office's designated bank account.

Revenue Accounting.q: Explain the formats used in revenue accounting.
Revenue Accounting.r: Pre-numbered receipt issued to the payer; the आम्दानी भौचर (revenue voucher) recording the head, payer, amount and evidence; the bank deposit slip; the bank cash book (No. 209); the monthly revenue statement; and the receipt-and-issue register in which the pre-numbered receipt books are issued and returned. Only the prescribed forms may be used.

Revenue Accounting.q: Write in brief about the revenue codes used in Nepal's government accounting, with examples.
Revenue Accounting.r: Revenue heads are coded in the uniform chart of accounts, and the code is the same in every district. The tax group is 11000 (11111 income tax on sole proprietorships and individuals). Non-tax revenue falls in 13000, 14000 and 15000 (14151 rent of government property, 14213 receipts from other sales, 14221 judicial fee, 14223 income from the education sector, 14224 examination fee, 14227 passport fee, 14251 company registration fee, 14252 agency registration fee, 14311 judicial fine). The early digits identify the group and the department, the later digits the individual head.

Revenue Accounting.q: A District Health Office collected the following revenue in the month of Falgun: 14213 other sales Rs. 41,000; 14223 income from the education sector Rs. 44,26,600; 14224 examination fee Rs. 1,75,500 of which Rs. 35,100 was not deposited; 14151 rent of government property Rs. 2,38,800. Prepare the revenue statement.
What is revenue accounting? Explain the banking arrangement and the reporting arrangement of revenue accounting in Nepal.
Revenue Accounting.r: Definition (2). As in Group A answer 1, with the point that revenue accounting is one of the areas of government accounting, alongside expenditure, store, fund and deposit accounting. Banking arrangement (3). Designated bank account under the single account fund; all revenue deposited into the consolidated fund through the Nepal Rastra Bank or a commercial bank; deposit on the same day of collection, or on the first working day with the reason recorded; no expense may be paid out of the collection; monthly bank reconciliation; supervision by the Treasury and Comptroller Office. Reporting arrangement (3). Daily entry in the bank cash book and checking of receipt counterfoils;

Revenue Accounting.q: What is a revenue statement? A District Administration Office collected the following revenue up to the month of Poush: 14151 rent of government property Rs. 2,38,800; 14213 other sales Rs. 41,000; 14223 education sector income Rs. 44,26,600; 14224 examination fee Rs. 1,75,500; 14227 passport fee Rs. 60,000. Of the examination fee Rs. 35,100 and of the passport fee Rs. 12,000 had not been deposited. Prepare the revenue statement and show how you verify it.
Revenue Accounting.r: Definition (1). The revenue statement is the prescribed monthly return showing head by head the revenue collected, the amount deposited into the consolidated fund and the cash balance in hand; its purpose is to prove that every rupee collected either reached the fund or is still held and accounted for. Preparation (5).

Revenue Accounting.q: What is revenue accounting? Explain its objectives, banking arrangement and reporting arrangement.

An office collected the following revenue during Ashad: vehicle tax Rs 1,20,000 (all deposited in the bank); fees and fines Rs 80,000 (Rs 75,000 deposited, the rest held in cash for the next working day); sale of old goods Rs 50,000 (all deposited). Prepare the revenue statement and explain how it is checked.

Accounting of Government Expenditure.q: Write the code for office materials and for furniture.
Write the number of the bank cash book format.
Write any two items entered on the debit side of the bank cash book.
Accounting of Government Expenditure.r: Any two of: budget release received; revenue deposited; retention and deductions received; refund of an unspent advance; amount transferred in.

Accounting of Government Expenditure.q: How is the available balance of a budget head found?
Accounting of Government Expenditure.r: Available balance = annual appropriation - total expenditure to date - uncleared advances.

Accounting of Government Expenditure.q: What is expenditure accounting? Explain the codes used in expenditure accounting.
Accounting of Government Expenditure.r: Expenditure accounting records what an office spends against its approved budget head, the advances it gives and recovers, the deductions it holds and its bank balance. Codes: the organisational classification says who spends; the economic classification says what — 2 recurrent (21111 remuneration, 21112 allowances, 21121 office materials, 22111 uniform, 22311 travelling expenses, 22612 fuel, 22711 miscellaneous) and 3 capital (31111 machinery and equipment, 31121 furniture, 31131 vehicles).

Accounting of Government Expenditure.q: What is a payment order? Explain the kinds of payment and the procedure for clearing an advance.
Accounting of Government Expenditure.r: A payment order is the document by which the office authorises the Treasury and Comptroller Office to pay a stated amount to a stated person against a stated head. Kinds: final (the bill has been received and checked) and advance (money needed before the bill). Clearing an advance: the advance is paid by payment order and entered in the advance register and the bank cash book; the officer later submits the bill with vouchers and any unspent balance; if the bill equals the advance it is cleared against the expenditure head; if larger, the excess is paid by a further payment order; if smaller, the unspent cash is refunded;

Accounting of Government Expenditure.q: What is the number of the bank cash book format?
Explain the formats used in expenditure accounting and reporting.
Accounting of Government Expenditure.r: Payment order — the authority to pay; vouchers — गोश्वारा भौचर for a transfer, निकासा भौचर for a payment, आम्दानी भौचर for a receipt, धरौटी भौचर for retention; advance register — advances and their clearance; bank cash book (No. 209) — the office's cash and bank record; head-wise ledger — appropriation, release and expenditure by head; statement of expenditure — the monthly return; deposit and retention ledgers — money held for others. Explain the purpose of each: to let a person who was not present reconstruct the transaction, and so to make it auditable.

Accounting of Government Expenditure.q: Explain budget release, budget transfer and re-appropriation.
Accounting of Government Expenditure.r: A budget release makes part of the appropriation available to the office, month by month or quarter by quarter; it is recorded by a निकासा भौचर and credited to the office's account, and the office may not spend more than the release. A budget transfer moves budget from one head to another or from one office to another with the approval of the prescribed authority. Re-appropriation moves savings from one head to another within the same office's budget, subject to the limits in the Financial Procedures Rules; amounts may not be taken out of protected heads such as remuneration, and re-appropriation may not be used to create a new item of expenditure that the legislature never approved.

Accounting of Government Expenditure.q: The following transactions relate to the District Administration Office, Rasuwa. Prepare the bank cash book for the month of Ashoj (no opening balance). 2082/06/01 payment order issued for house rent Rs. 10,000; 06/05 advance given to Mr. Rai for the purchase of office furniture Rs. 50,000; 06/12 budget release received from the DTCO Rs. 3,00,000; 06/15 Mr. Rai's advance cleared on a furniture bill of Rs. 58,000, the excess paid by payment order; 06/22 salary payment order for the month issued after deducting provident fund Rs. 20,000 and income tax Rs. 3,000 out of a total salary of Rs. 1,80,000; 06/28 the deductions deposited into the concerned office.

What is the bank cash book (म.ले.प.फा.नं. २०९)? Prepare it from the following transactions of an office for Shrawan: opening balance Rs 1,50,000; 5th budget release received Rs 8,00,000; 12th salary paid Rs 3,20,000; 15th office supplies Rs 45,000; 20th advance to a staff member Rs 60,000; 28th refund of an advance Rs 10,000; 30th tax deducted at source deposited Rs 18,000.
Explain the payment order, advance and clearance, and budget release, transfer and re-appropriation.
In the context of government accounting, what does the term 'virement' refer to?
o: Transfer of funds between different heads of accounts within the same department.
Increase in the allocated budget mid-year without parliamentary approval.
Reduction in the total expenditure of the government.
Allocation of funds for unforeseen expenditures.
Accounting of Government Expenditure.w: Virement refers to the internal reallocation of funds within a department's budget without changing the total amount appropriated.

Accounting of Government Expenditure.q: According to the rules of government accounting, how is the payment of salaries categorized?
Accounting of Government Expenditure.w: Salaries paid by the government fall under revenue expenditure as they are regular payments for services rendered.

Store Accounting.q: Write any two importance of store accounting.
Store Accounting.r: Any two of: to record every receipt and issue; to show the stock balance at any time; to prevent loss, misuse and theft; to provide audit evidence; to help budgeting.

Store Accounting.q: Write any two examples of durable store goods.
Store Accounting.r: Any two of: furniture, computers, vehicles, machines, musical instruments.

Store Accounting.q: What is the जिन्सी दाखिला फाराम used for?
Store Accounting.r: For recording goods received into the store — date, description, specification, quantity, value and supplier.

Store Accounting.q: Who conducts the physical verification of a government store?
Store Accounting.r: A store inspection committee of at least two officers, one of whom is not connected with the store.

Store Accounting.q: With which record must the bin card always agree?
What is store accounting? Explain its objectives and importance.
Store Accounting.r: Store accounting records the receipt, storage, issue and balance of goods held by a government office, in quantity and in value; the goods are consumable (stationery, fuel, medicines) or durable (furniture, computers, vehicles). Objectives: to record every receipt and issue; to show the balance at any time; to prevent loss and misuse; to provide audit evidence; to help budgeting. Importance: public goods remain public property; each article is tied to a document and a person; the honest officer is protected; the annual verification rests on it.

Store Accounting.q: Explain the main formats used in store accounting.
Store Accounting.r: जिन्सी दाखिला फाराम — goods received, with specification, quantity, value, supplier and purchase voucher; जिन्सी निकासा फाराम — goods issued, with the requisition and the receiver's signature; store ledger — one account per article with receipts, issues and balance; bin card — the same record kept at the shelf; जिन्सी मौज्दात फाँटबारी — the periodic stock statement; जिन्सी जाँच फाराम — the physical verification record; the voucher that brings the store figures into the accounts.

Store Accounting.q: Explain the use of the store account and the procedure of store verification.
Store Accounting.r: Use: the storekeeper reads it to know what to requisition; the accounts section to value the goods and enter them in the accounts; the auditor to trace an article from the purchase bill to the store ledger, to the bin card and to the shelf. Verification: an annual physical count by a committee of at least two officers, one unconnected with the store; the count is compared with the ledger and the bin card; differences are recorded in the verification form; an excess is brought into account, a shortage is recovered from the person responsible or written off with approval, and unserviceable goods are written off and disposed of in the prescribed manner.

Store Accounting.q: What is a store ledger? Explain its form with a suitable example.
Store Accounting.r: The store ledger is the principal store book with one account or page per article. It carries the date, the particulars, the receipt quantity, the issue quantity and the balance, and it is usually kept in the continuous balance form so that the balance is visible after every entry. Give an example: receive 50 units, issue 10 (balance 40), receive 25 (balance 65), issue 15 (balance 50), and value the closing stock at the purchase rate.

Store Accounting.q: The store of a government office holds steel chairs. On Kartik 1, 40 chairs were received at Rs. 2,500 each. On Kartik 8, 12 were issued to the administration section; on Kartik 18, 20 more were received; on Kartik 25, 8 were issued to the examination section. Prepare the store ledger and find the value of the closing stock.
What is store accounting? Explain its objectives, importance and the main store formats, and describe how a government store is verified.
Store Accounting.r: Definition (1). As in Group A answer 1. Objectives and importance (3). Record every receipt and issue with evidence; show the balance at any time; prevent loss and misuse; provide audit evidence; help budgeting. Importance: public goods stay public property; each article is tied to a document and a person; the honest officer is protected; the annual verification and the stock statement rest on it. Formats (2). जिन्सी दाखिला फाराम, जिन्सी निकासा फाराम, store ledger, bin card, stock statement, verification form and the voucher — one line each. Verification (2). Annual physical count by a store inspection committee of at least two officers, one unconnected with the store;

Store Accounting.q: Explain the meaning of जिन्सी, the two kinds of store goods, and the procedure by which goods are received into and issued from a government store.
Store Accounting.r: Meaning (1). जिन्सी means the goods and articles held by a government office, and जिन्सी लेखा is the account of their receipt, storage, issue and balance in quantity and value. Two kinds (2). Consumable goods, used up in the course of work — stationery, ink, cleaning materials, medicines, fuel; and non-consumable or durable goods, which keep their identity and are used over years — furniture, computers, vehicles, machines. Consumable goods are expensed, while durable goods are capital expenditure and remain on the store record. Receipt (2). Goods are bought by a payment order against a budget head;

Store Accounting.q: What is store (जिन्सी) accounting? Explain its objectives and importance in eight points.

Explain the formats used in store accounting and the annual store verification. Show the entries of a store ledger (bin card) from the data given: opening balance 100 reams of paper; 6th received 60; 10th issued 45; 18th issued 35; 25th received 40; 28th issued 50.
In store accounting, what does the term 'stock-in-hand' refer to?
o: The total amount of stock sold during a period
The quantity of stock available at the end of an accounting period
The cost of goods manufactured during the period
The projected stock needed for the next period
Store Accounting.w: Stock-in-hand represents the physical inventory count of items available at the end of an accounting period.

Store Accounting.q: Which of the following best describes the purpose of a bin card in store accounting?
o: To record the financial transactions related to sales
To track the movement of specific stock items
To calculate the depreciation of assets
To monitor the company's cash flow
Store Accounting.w: A bin card is a document used to keep track of the movement of specific stock items in a warehouse.

Store Accounting.q: What is the role of a perpetual inventory system in store accounting?
o: It updates inventory records after every transaction
It provides a monthly summary of inventory levels
It calculates the total value of all unsold goods annually
It records the supplier's credit terms
Store Accounting.w: A perpetual inventory system automatically updates inventory records after every transaction involving the purchase or sale of inventory.

Fund Accounting and Retention Account.q: Which body recommends the shares of the divisible fund?
Fund Accounting and Retention Account.r: The National Natural Resources and Fiscal Commission.

Fund Accounting and Retention Account.q: Show the retention journal voucher at the time the retention money is received (deducted).
Fund Accounting and Retention Account.r: Construction (or supplies) expenditure A/c Dr. (full bill); To Contractors' retention A/c (the amount withheld); To Bank / DTCO A/c (the net paid).

Fund Accounting and Retention Account.q: Is retention revenue? Give one reason.
Fund Accounting and Retention Account.r: No. It is a liability of the office to the party from whom it was withheld; it must be returned, or forfeited to revenue only if the condition is not met.

Fund Accounting and Retention Account.q: What is a fund? Explain the need for fund accounting in government.
Fund Accounting and Retention Account.r: A fund is a separate pool of money set aside for a specified purpose and accounted for separately. Need: to obey the law that creates each fund; to prevent money of one fund being used for another purpose; to make control by the legislature and the auditor possible; to keep trust money such as retention, provident fund and tax deducted out of revenue; and to plan a project fund by showing what has accumulated and what is still needed.

Fund Accounting and Retention Account.q: What is revenue sharing? Explain its importance in a federal Nepal.
Fund Accounting and Retention Account.r: Revenue sharing is the distribution of the divisible fund — the federal taxes to be shared, principally VAT, income tax and royalties — between the provinces and the local levels on the recommendation of the National Natural Resources and Fiscal Commission and under a formula based on population, area, development and revenue effort. Importance: it gives the lower tiers the money for their constitutional work although the main taxes are collected federally; it reduces inequality between regions; it strengthens federalism; it rewards local revenue effort; and it keeps the tax system uniform.

Fund Accounting and Retention Account.q: A contractor's bill of Rs. 4,00,000 is passed and a retention of 5 per cent is withheld. After the defect liability period the retention is released. Show the journal vouchers.
Fund Accounting and Retention Account.r: Retention $= 5\% \times 4{,}00{,}000 = Rs.\ 20{,}000$; net paid $= Rs.\ 3{,}80{,}000$. When the bill is passed: Construction expenditure A/c Dr. 4,00,000; To Contractors' retention A/c 20,000; To Bank / DTCO A/c 3,80,000. When released: Contractors' retention A/c Dr. 20,000; To Bank A/c 20,000.

Fund Accounting and Retention Account.q: Write the name of the book in which retention held for others is kept.
Fund Accounting and Retention Account.r: The retention ledger (धरौटी खाता), supported by the retention bank cash book.

Fund Accounting and Retention Account.q: What is the consolidated fund? Explain the provisions for its operation.
Fund Accounting and Retention Account.r: Definition as in Group A answer 3. Provisions: all government receipts must be credited to it; no payment without an appropriation act; expenditure only for the approved purpose; unforeseen expenditure met from the contingency fund and later regularised; managed by the Ministry of Finance and accounted for by the FCGO, the money kept with the Nepal Rastra Bank and other banks; annual financial statement laid before the legislature and audited by the Office of the Auditor General; only the authorised officer may draw, and only within the release received.

Fund Accounting and Retention Account.q: What is retention accounting? Explain the three kinds of retention and the formats used.
Fund Accounting and Retention Account.r: Retention accounting is the branch that records money withheld from a payment and held until a condition is met, and its later release, adjustment or forfeiture. Kinds: goods retention — withheld on the purchase of goods until supply and acceptance; works retention — withheld from a construction bill until the end of the defect liability period; personal retention — held on behalf of a person, such as provident fund, income tax deducted at source and the citizen investment trust. Formats: the धरौटी भौचर for the deduction, the धरौटी खाता (retention ledger) with one account per party, the personal and general retention ledgers, and the retention bank cash book.

Fund Accounting and Retention Account.q: A contractor's bill of Rs. 5,00,000 is passed and retention of 5 per cent is withheld. After the defect liability period the retention is released. Show the journal vouchers.
Fund Accounting and Retention Account.r: Retention $= 5\% \times 5{,}00{,}000 = Rs.\ 25{,}000$; net paid $= Rs.\ 4{,}75{,}000$. When the bill is passed: Construction expenditure A/c Dr. 5,00,000 To Contractors' retention A/c 25,000 To Bank / DTCO A/c 4,75,000 (Being the running bill passed and retention of 5 per cent withheld.) When the retention is released: Contractors' retention A/c Dr. 25,000 To Bank A/c 25,000 (Being the retention money released to the contractor on the expiry of the defect liability period.)

Fund Accounting and Retention Account.q: What is retention accounting? Explain the three kinds of retention and, with journal vouchers, show how retention is recorded when it is withheld on a contractor's bill, when it is released, and when it is forfeited after a defect is not remedied.
Fund Accounting and Retention Account.r: Definition and nature (2). Retention is money withheld from a payment due to a contractor, supplier or employee and held until a condition is satisfied; it is a liability, not revenue and not an expenditure. Kinds (2). Goods retention, works retention and personal retention (provident fund, income tax deducted, citizen investment trust), each explained in a sentence. Formats (1). धरौटी भौचर, धरौटी खाता with one account per party, personal and general retention ledgers, retention bank cash book. Journal vouchers (3). (i) When the bill is passed and retention withheld: expenditure A/c Dr. (full bill); To Contractors' retention A/c (amount withheld); To Bank/DTCO A/c (net paid).

Fund Accounting and Retention Account.q: What is a fund? Explain the consolidated fund and the divisible fund, and the importance of revenue sharing.

What is retention money? A contractor's bill is Rs 4,00,000. Retention of 5% and income tax of 1.5% are deducted at source. Find the net payment and pass the entries, and explain the kinds of retention.
In fund accounting, which type of fund is typically used by a government to manage its general operating expenses?
Fund Accounting and Retention Account.w: The General Fund is used for managing general operating expenses and is not restricted for any specific purpose.

Fund Accounting and Retention Account.q: What does the retention account represent in financial statements?
o: The total amount of dividends paid to shareholders
The cumulative earnings reinvested in the business
The total revenue earned during a fiscal year
The total liabilities owed to creditors
Fund Accounting and Retention Account.w: Retention account represents the earnings kept within the company that have not been distributed as dividends.

Fund Accounting and Retention Account.q: In the context of fund accounting, which statement best describes the purpose of a special revenue fund?
o: To manage resources for long-term capital assets
To account for taxes and other revenues that are legally restricted to specific purposes
To provide liquidity for daily operational needs
Fund Accounting and Retention Account.w: Special revenue funds are used to account for revenues that are legally restricted to specific purposes, ensuring these resources are used appropriately.

Internal Control and Auditing.q: Write any two objectives of internal control.
Internal Control and Auditing.r: Any two of: to safeguard assets; to keep the records accurate and complete; to secure efficiency; to ensure compliance with the law; to prevent and detect fraud and error; to make an audit possible.

Internal Control and Auditing.q: Write any two elements of internal control.
Internal Control and Auditing.r: Any two of: segregation of duties; authorisation; documentation; physical control; reconciliation; supervision; rotation and compulsory leave; internal audit; budget comparison.

Internal Control and Auditing.q: Write any two types of audit on the basis of object.
Internal Control and Auditing.r: Any two of: financial (regularity) audit, performance audit, management audit, propriety audit.

Internal Control and Auditing.q: Which is the apex auditing body of Nepal?
Internal Control and Auditing.r: The Office of the Auditor General (महालेखापरीक्षकको कार्यालय).

Internal Control and Auditing.q: Name the parliamentary committee that examines the audit report.
Internal Control and Auditing.r: The Public Accounts Committee (सार्वजनिक लेखा समिति).

Internal Control and Auditing.q: Who appoints the Auditor General of Nepal?
Internal Control and Auditing.r: The President, on the recommendation of the Constitutional Council.

Internal Control and Auditing.q: What is internal control? Explain its objectives.
Internal Control and Auditing.r: Internal control is the whole system of policies, procedures, records and checks by which an organisation keeps its work accurate, efficient, lawful and honest and protects its assets. Objectives: to safeguard assets; to keep the records accurate and complete; to secure efficiency; to ensure compliance with the law and the budget; to prevent and detect fraud and error; to make an audit possible.

Internal Control and Auditing.q: Distinguish between internal audit and final audit.
Internal Control and Auditing.r: Internal audit: conducted by an employee; continuous through the year; reports to the management or the audit committee; its main object is to test internal control; independence is limited; interim reports with recommendations. Final audit: conducted by an independent external auditor; after the year end; reports to the owners or the legislature; its main object is to express an opinion on the truth and fairness of the accounts; independence is full; one statutory report with an opinion.

Internal Control and Auditing.q: Who is the apex auditing body in Nepal? Explain what it audits and what happens to its report.
Internal Control and Auditing.r: The Office of the Auditor General (महालेखापरीक्षकको कार्यालय), a constitutional body headed by the Auditor General, appointed by the President on the recommendation of the Constitutional Council and removable only in the manner provided for a Supreme Court judge. It audits the federal ministries, departments and offices; the provinces and local levels; the constitutional bodies and courts; government corporations and grant-receiving offices; foreign loans and grants; and the stores and assets as well as the money.
The employees of the organisation itself, working under the management or the audit committee.

Internal Control and Auditing.q: Name the parliamentary committee that examines the audit report in Nepal.
Internal Control and Auditing.r: The Public Accounts Committee (सार्वजनिक लेखा समिति).

Internal Control and Auditing.q: Explain any five elements of a good internal control system.
Internal Control and Auditing.r: (i) Segregation of duties — the person who authorises, the person who pays and the person who records must be different. (ii) Authorisation — every payment and entry needs the signature of the competent officer. (iii) Documentation — pre-numbered prescribed forms with evidence attached. (iv) Physical control — locked store and cash box, restricted access, custody with named persons. (v) Reconciliation — monthly bank reconciliation, store ledger against bin card, physical verification. (Also: supervision, rotation and compulsory leave, internal audit, budget comparison.)

Internal Control and Auditing.q: Explain the types of audit on the basis of time, scope and object.
Internal Control and Auditing.r: By time: continuous (throughout the year), interim (during the year for part of the period), final (after the year end on the completed accounts). By scope: complete (all the books), partial (a part), special (a particular matter on a special order). By object: financial or regularity (are the accounts true and the rules followed), performance or value-for-money (was the money spent economically and efficiently), management (are the systems and decisions sound), propriety (is the transaction proper and above suspicion).

Internal Control and Auditing.q: What is internal control? Explain its objectives and elements, and show what would go wrong in an office where the same clerk receives cash, writes the receipt, records it and reconciles the bank.
Internal Control and Auditing.r: Definition (1). As in Group A answer 1. Objectives (3). Safeguard assets; accurate and complete records; efficiency; compliance with law and budget; prevention and detection of fraud and error; a basis for audit. Explain each in one sentence. Elements (2). Segregation of duties, authorisation, documentation, physical control, reconciliation, supervision, rotation and compulsory leave, internal audit, budget comparison — any five or six explained. The danger of one pair of hands (2).

Internal Control and Auditing.q: What is auditing? Explain the meaning of internal control and audit, the types of audit, and the government audit system of Nepal including the Office of the Auditor General and the settlement of audit observations.
Internal Control and Auditing.r: Auditing (2). Definition as in Group A answer 4, with the three features — independence, examination of evidence, and the expression of an opinion rather than a guarantee. Internal control and the types of audit (3). Internal control as the system of checks; internal and external audit; continuous, interim and final audit; complete, partial and special audit; and by object the financial, performance, management and propriety audits. Distinguish an internal audit (an employee, continuous, reports to management, tests control, limited independence) from a final audit (an independent outsider, after the year end, reports to the owners or the legislature, gives an opinion).

Internal Control and Auditing.q: What is internal control? Explain its objectives and elements, and show why one clerk should not control a whole transaction.
What is auditing? Explain its types, and the government audit by the Office of the Auditor General.

Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.q: Which office prepares the annual budget of the Government of Nepal?
Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.r: The Ministry of Finance.

Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.q: Write any two functions of the Ministry of Finance.
Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.r: Any two of: preparing the budget; framing revenue and fiscal policy; managing the consolidated fund; arranging loans and grants; controlling public expenditure; fixing the terms of government borrowing.

Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.q: What is the full form of FCGO and what does it do?
Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.r: Financial Comptroller General Office (महालेखा नियन्त्रक कार्यालय); it releases the budget, keeps the central accounts, supervises the Treasury and Comptroller Offices, consolidates the accounts, maintains the chart of accounts and the formats, and operates the computerised systems.

Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.q: What is a DTCO and what does it do?
Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.r: The District Treasury and Comptroller Office; it receives the budget release and makes the payments of the government offices in the district on their payment orders, and keeps the operating level accounts.

Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.q: Which office releases the budget to a spending office?
Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.r: The Financial Comptroller General Office, through the Treasury and Comptroller Office.

Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.q: Who is the banker to the Government of Nepal?
Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.r: Nepal Rastra Bank.

Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.q: What is the function of the National Planning Commission?
Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.r: The National Planning Commission prepares the country's periodic development plan, sets the priorities and sectoral ceilings for the budget, appraises large projects and recommends the resource envelope.

Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.q: Name the two names of government offices that use central level accounting.
Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.r: The Ministry of Finance and the Office of the Auditor General (also acceptable: a ministry or department at the centre, and the FCGO).

Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.q: What is the single account fund?
Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.r: The arrangement under which a government office keeps one designated bank account for all its receipts and payments, recorded in the bank cash book, under the Treasury Single Account.

Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.q: Name the agencies involved in the government accounting system of Nepal and explain the functions of any four.
Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.r: Agencies: Ministry of Finance; National Planning Commission; Financial Comptroller General Office; Treasury and Comptroller Offices; the spending offices; Office of the Auditor General; Public Accounts Committee; Nepal Rastra Bank. Explain any four: Ministry of Finance — budget, fiscal policy, consolidated fund, loans and grants, expenditure control; FCGO — release, central accounts, consolidation, formats and systems; DTCO — payments, operating level accounts, single account fund, reporting; Office of the Auditor General — audit of all government accounts and stores and report to the President and Parliament.

Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.q: Explain the functions of the Financial Comptroller General Office.
Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.r: The FCGO is the office under the Ministry of Finance that runs the government accounting system. Functions: releasing the budget to spending offices against the appropriation; keeping the central accounts; supervising and guiding the Treasury and Comptroller Offices; consolidating the accounts of all offices and preparing the annual financial statement and periodical reports; maintaining the uniform chart of accounts and the prescribed formats; and operating the computerised systems (FMIS, CGAS, TSA, SUTRA).

Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.q: Explain the banking arrangement of government offices.
Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.r: One designated bank account per office under the single account fund; the release credited directly to it; payment by cheque or electronic transfer on a payment order, not in cash except for allowed petty expenses; revenue deposited the same day and never spent; every entry in the bank cash book and a monthly bank reconciliation sent with the statement of expenditure; no overdraft and no idle balances; strict custody of cheque books. The arrangement makes the government's cash position knowable, keeps expenditure within the budget and makes reconciliation possible.

Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.q: What is the role of the Financial Comptroller General Office?
Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.r: The Financial Comptroller General Office releases the budget, keeps the central accounts, supervises the Treasury and Comptroller Offices, consolidates the accounts of all offices, maintains the chart of accounts and the formats, and operates the computerised accounting systems.

Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.q: What is the full form of FCGO?
Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.r: Financial Comptroller General Office (महालेखा नियन्त्रक कार्यालय).

Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.q: Explain the functions of the Ministry of Finance.
Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.r: Preparing the budget and the annual financial statement; framing revenue and tax policy and fiscal policy; managing the consolidated fund and the contingency fund; arranging internal and external loans, grants and foreign aid; controlling and monitoring public expenditure; fixing the terms of government borrowing and advising on the exchange rate policy with Nepal Rastra Bank; laying the annual report of the FCGO before the legislature; and representing the government in financial negotiations.

Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.q: What is the Financial Comptroller General Office? Explain its functions.
Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.r: The FCGO is the office under the Ministry of Finance that runs the government accounting system. Functions: releasing the budget to spending offices against the appropriation; keeping the central accounts; supervising and guiding the Treasury and Comptroller Offices; consolidating the accounts of all offices and preparing the annual financial statement and the periodical reports; maintaining the uniform chart of accounts and the prescribed formats; and operating the computerised systems (FMIS, CGAS, TSA, SUTRA).

Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.q: Explain the functions of the Treasury and Comptroller Offices.
Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.r: Receiving the budget release from the FCGO and passing it to the offices in its jurisdiction; making payments on the offices' payment orders by cheque or electronic transfer; keeping the operating level accounts and consolidating the monthly statements of expenditure; controlling expenditure against the release and refusing defective payment orders; operating the single account fund in the district; making the bank reconciliation and reporting the financial position to the FCGO; and receiving and forwarding revenue deposits to the consolidated fund.

Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.q: Explain the role of the Public Accounts Committee and of Nepal Rastra Bank in the government accounting system.
Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.r: The Public Accounts Committee is a committee of the legislature that examines the report of the Auditor General, calls the Secretary or head of the office concerned to explain each observation, takes evidence, directs the recovery of money or the correction of the system and reports to the House — it turns an audit observation into an action. Nepal Rastra Bank is the banker to the government: it keeps the government's and the offices' accounts, receives government revenue and makes payments through the Treasury and Comptroller Offices, holds the foreign exchange reserves and manages the issue of treasury bills and bonds by which the government borrows.

Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.q: Explain the agencies involved in the government accounting system of Nepal and their functions, and describe the banking arrangement of government offices.
Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.r: The agencies (4). Ministry of Finance (budget, fiscal policy, consolidated fund, loans and grants, expenditure control); National Planning Commission (plan, priorities, ceilings, project appraisal); FCGO (release, central accounts, consolidation, chart of accounts, computerised systems); Treasury and Comptroller Offices (payments, operating level accounts, single account fund, reporting); the spending offices (incur expenditure and keep primary records); Office of the Auditor General (audit); Public Accounts Committee (examination of the report and action); Nepal Rastra Bank (banker to the government). Give the function of each in a sentence or two. Banking arrangement (4).

Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.q: Explain the government accounting system of Nepal from the preparation of the budget to the settlement of the audit report, naming the agency responsible at each stage.
Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.r: Budget preparation (1). The National Planning Commission sets the plan, the priorities and the sectoral ceilings; the Ministry of Finance prepares the budget and the annual financial statement, with the line ministries feeding their proposals through the LMBIS. Authorisation (1). The budget is presented to Parliament, discussed and passed as the Appropriation Act and the Finance Act; without these, nothing may be spent or collected. Release (1). The FCGO releases money to the spending offices through the Treasury and Comptroller Offices, and the release is credited to the office's account under the single account fund. Execution (2). The spending office spends against a budget head;

Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.q: Explain the agencies involved in government accounting in Nepal and the function of each.
Explain the banking arrangement of government offices, and trace the path of a budget from preparation to audit.
Which agency is primarily responsible for managing the budgetary allocations and expenditures of the government?
Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.w: The Ministry of Finance is responsible for managing the budgetary allocations and expenditures of the government.

Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.q: What role does the Comptroller General's Office play in government accounting?
o: Conducting external audits of government finances
Overseeing the financial transactions and accounts of the government ministries and departments
Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.w: The Comptroller General's Office oversees the financial transactions and accounts of the government ministries and departments.

Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.q: In the context of government accounting, which body has the authority to approve the annual budget?
Agencies Involved in Government Accounti.w: Parliament has the authority to approve the annual budget in the context of government accounting.

Use of Information Technology in Office.q: Write any two components of an information system.
Use of Information Technology in Office.r: Any two of: hardware, software, network, data, people, procedures.

Use of Information Technology in Office.q: What is an office package? Write any two names.
Use of Information Technology in Office.r: An office package is a set of application software that does the ordinary work of an office; examples are Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Access.

Use of Information Technology in Office.q: Write any two advantages of information technology.
Use of Information Technology in Office.r: Any two of: speed; accuracy; storage and retrieval; automatic posting; instant reporting; communication; less paper; better control.

Use of Information Technology in Office.q: Write any two disadvantages of information technology.
Use of Information Technology in Office.r: Any two of: cost; dependence; data loss; fraud and hacking; training; unemployment; health problems; garbage in garbage out; obsolescence.

Use of Information Technology in Office.q: Name any two accounting software used in Nepal.
Use of Information Technology in Office.r: Any two of: Tally, Swastik, Easy Account, Quick Book.

Use of Information Technology in Office.q: Write the full form of LMBIS or SUTRA.
Use of Information Technology in Office.r: LMBIS — Line Ministry Budget Information System; SUTRA — Sub-National Treasury Regulatory Application.

Use of Information Technology in Office.q: What is information technology? Explain its main components and any three office packages used in an office.
Use of Information Technology in Office.r: Information technology is the whole set of devices, software, networks and methods by which information is collected, stored, processed and communicated.
