History of Computer.w: the first was accepted by the US Census Bureau in 1951.

History of Computer.q: What were Napier's bones? Who invented them and when?
History of Computer.r: Napier's bones were a set of numbered rods (strips) used for multiplication, by reading and adding the numbers on the rods placed side by side. They were invented by the Scottish mathematician John Napier in 1617.

History of Computer.q: Differentiate between the Pascaline and Leibniz's stepped reckoner.
History of Computer.r: The Pascaline (Blaise Pascal, 1642) used toothed wheels with automatic carry and could only add and subtract. The stepped reckoner (Gottfried Leibniz, 1673) could do all four operations: add, subtract, multiply and divide.

History of Computer.q: Why is the Jacquard loom important in the history of computers?
History of Computer.r: In 1804 Joseph Marie Jacquard's loom used punched cards to control the pattern woven into cloth. It was the first machine controlled by stored instructions on cards — the idea Babbage used for the Analytical Engine and Hollerith for his tabulator.

History of Computer.q: Write short notes on ENIAC and UNIVAC I.
History of Computer.r: ENIAC (Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer), 1946: the first general-purpose electronic digital computer, built in the USA with 17,468 vacuum tubes; it was huge, used a lot of electricity and was programmed by setting switches and cables. UNIVAC I (Universal Automatic Computer), 1951: the first computer sold commercially in the USA; it used vacuum tubes and magnetic tape and processed the US census.

History of Computer.q: Describe the history of computers in Nepal.
History of Computer.r: (1) In 2028 BS (1971 AD) an IBM 1401, a second-generation computer, was brought to Nepal on rent (Rs 1,25,000 a month) to process the census of 2028 BS. (2) In 2031 BS the Electronic Data Processing Centre was set up; it later became the National Computer Centre (NCC). (3) In 2038 BS the ICL 2950/10 mainframe, with 64 terminals, came for the census of 2038 BS. (4) From 2039–2040 BS microcomputers such as Apple were imported by private companies; the Internet came in 2052 BS (1995), and today computers are used in every bank, office and school.

History of Computer.w: heaven beads are worth 5; earth beads 1.

History of Computer.w: Atanasoff and Berry at Iowa State College.

History of Computer.q: What is an abacus? Write the value of a heaven bead and an earth bead on a suanpan.
History of Computer.r: An abacus is a hand-operated counting device: a frame with rods on which beads slide, used for addition and subtraction. On a suanpan each heaven bead (above the beam) is worth 5 and each earth bead (below) is worth 1.

History of Computer.q: Show how Napier's bones give 46 × 7.
History of Computer.r: Place bones 4 and 6 side by side and read row 7: 2|8 and 4|2. Add the diagonals from the right: 2; 8 + 4 = 12, write 2 carry 1; 2 + 1 = 3. Answer: 322.

History of Computer.q: Why is Charles Babbage called the father of the computer?
History of Computer.r: Because his Analytical Engine (1834) was the first design for a general-purpose, programmable computer, and it had input (punched cards), a mill (processor), a store (memory) and output — the same units as modern computers.

History of Computer.q: Why is Ada Lovelace called the first programmer?
History of Computer.r: In 1843 she wrote notes on Babbage's Analytical Engine in which she set out step by step how the engine would calculate Bernoulli numbers. This is the first published computer program; she also foresaw that computers could work with symbols and music, not only numbers.

History of Computer.q: How did the Jacquard loom influence the development of computers?
History of Computer.r: The loom (1804) was controlled by punched cards: the pattern of holes decided the woven pattern. This showed that instructions could be stored on cards and changed without changing the machine; Babbage used the idea for the Analytical Engine and Hollerith for his census tabulator.

History of Computer.q: Write the full forms of EDVAC, UNIVAC, ABC and EDSAC.
History of Computer.r: EDVAC — Electronic Discrete Variable Automatic Computer; UNIVAC — Universal Automatic Computer; ABC — Atanasoff–Berry Computer; EDSAC — Electronic Delay Storage Automatic Calculator.

History of Computer.q: What is the stored-program concept? Why was it an improvement on ENIAC?
History of Computer.r: The stored-program concept (von Neumann, 1945) keeps the program's instructions in memory with the data. ENIAC had to be re-wired by hand to change its program, which took days; a stored-program computer just loads new instructions.

History of Computer.q: Write a short note on the IBM 1401 in Nepal.
History of Computer.r: The IBM 1401, a second-generation computer, was Nepal's first computer. It was brought on rent in 2028 BS (1971 AD), at Rs 1,25,000 a month, to process the census of 2028 BS at the Central Bureau of Statistics.

History of Computer.q: Describe the abacus, Napier's bones and the slide rule.
History of Computer.r: Abacus: the oldest calculating device (counting boards in Mesopotamia c. 2700 BC; the Chinese suanpan later). A frame of rods with beads; a beam divides heaven beads (worth 5) from earth beads (worth 1); beads moved to the beam are counted; used for addition and subtraction. Napier's bones: John Napier, Scotland, 1617. Rods for the digits 0–9, each carrying the multiples of its digit in squares split by a diagonal; placing rods side by side and adding along the diagonals gives a product. Slide rule: William Oughtred, c. 1622, based on Napier's logarithms. Two logarithmic scales slide past each other to multiply and divide;

History of Computer.q: Describe Babbage's Analytical Engine and explain why it is important.
History of Computer.r: Designed by Charles Babbage from 1834 as a general-purpose machine driven by steam. Its parts: input by punched cards (from the Jacquard loom) for numbers and operations; the mill, which did the arithmetic; the store, which held 1,000 numbers; and output by printer, curve plotter and bell. It could make decisions and repeat steps. It was never completed, for lack of money and precise engineering. Importance: it was the first design of a programmable computer, and its plan — input, processor, memory, output — is still the plan of every computer; Ada Lovelace wrote the first program for it. That is why Babbage is called the father of the computer.

Write about Charles Babbage and Ada Lovelace. Describe how computers came to Nepal.

Generations of Computer.q: Write any two features of first-generation computers.
Generations of Computer.r: Any two: they used vacuum tubes; they were huge, heavy and gave off great heat; they used a lot of electricity and failed often; they were programmed in machine language; their speed was measured in milliseconds.

Generations of Computer.q: What is a transistor? Write one advantage it had over the vacuum tube.
Generations of Computer.r: A transistor is a small electronic switch made of a semiconductor (invented at Bell Labs in 1947). Compared with a vacuum tube, it is far smaller, uses less electricity, gives off less heat and is more reliable.

Generations of Computer.q: What is an integrated circuit? Which generation used it first?
Generations of Computer.r: An integrated circuit (IC, or chip) is a small piece of silicon on which many transistors and other components are made together. ICs were first used in the third generation (about 1964–1975).

Generations of Computer.q: What is a microprocessor? Name the first microprocessor and its year.
Generations of Computer.r: A microprocessor is a single chip that contains the whole CPU of a computer. The first was the Intel 4004, made in 1971.

Generations of Computer.q: Compare the second and third generations of computers in four points.
Explain fifth-generation computers: their technology, features and uses.
Generations of Computer.r: (1) Technology: artificial intelligence (AI) — computers that learn, reason and understand language — and parallel processing, in which many processors work on parts of a problem at the same time. (2) Features: they can understand natural (spoken and written) language, recognise faces and speech, and learn from data. (3) Uses: voice assistants, translation apps, self-driving cars, medical diagnosis, robots. (4) Research continues in quantum computing; this generation is still developing.

Generations of Computer.q: First-generation computers used
The transistor was invented in 1947 at
Generations of Computer.w: Bardeen, Brattain and Shockley at Bell Labs.

Generations of Computer.q: Which generation used magnetic core memory and assembly language?
Generations of Computer.w: core memory and assembly language came with transistors.

Generations of Computer.q: The integrated circuit was invented by
The first microprocessor was the
The computers we use at school belong to the
What is meant by a generation of computer?
Generations of Computer.r: A generation of computer is a stage in the development of computers marked by a major new technology, especially a new main processing component. Each new generation was smaller, faster, cheaper, more reliable and more powerful than the one before.

Generations of Computer.q: Write any four features of first-generation computers.
Generations of Computer.r: Any four: vacuum tubes as the main component; magnetic drum memory; machine language; punched cards and paper tape for input; huge size; much heat and electricity; unreliable; slow (milliseconds); very expensive.

Generations of Computer.q: What is a transistor? Why was it better than a vacuum tube?
Generations of Computer.r: A transistor is a small semiconductor component that switches and amplifies electric current. It was better because it was much smaller, used less power, gave off little heat, was faster and lasted longer, so computers became smaller, cheaper and more reliable.

Generations of Computer.q: What is an integrated circuit? Who invented it?
Generations of Computer.r: An integrated circuit (chip) is a complete circuit of many transistors, resistors and capacitors made on one small piece of silicon. It was invented by Jack Kilby (1958), and independently by Robert Noyce (1959).

Generations of Computer.q: What is a microprocessor? Name the first microprocessor.
Generations of Computer.r: A microprocessor is a single chip that contains the whole CPU (control unit, ALU and registers). The first was the Intel 4004 (1971).

Generations of Computer.q: Write the full forms of IC, LSI, VLSI and ULSI.
Generations of Computer.r: IC — Integrated Circuit; LSI — Large Scale Integration; VLSI — Very Large Scale Integration; ULSI — Ultra Large Scale Integration.

Generations of Computer.q: What is artificial intelligence? Give two examples of its use.
Generations of Computer.r: AI is the ability of a computer program to do tasks that need human intelligence, such as understanding language, recognising faces, learning and deciding. Examples: voice assistants, face unlock, Google Translate, AI chatbots, self-driving cars (any two).

Generations of Computer.q: What is parallel processing? Give one example.
Generations of Computer.r: Parallel processing divides a big task into parts that several processors work on at the same time, so it finishes faster. Example: a supercomputer running a weather forecast on thousands of processors, or the eight cores of a phone processor.

Generations of Computer.q: A job takes 48 hours on one processor. Ideally, how long will it take on 6 processors? Why is the real time longer?
Generations of Computer.r: Ideal time = 48 ÷ 6 = 8 hours. It is longer in practice because the processors must share out the work, wait for each other and combine results, and some steps cannot be split.

Generations of Computer.q: Describe the features of second-generation computers with examples.
Generations of Computer.r: Period about 1958–1964. Main component: transistors (invented at Bell Labs in 1947) instead of vacuum tubes. Magnetic core memory; magnetic tape and disks for storage. Assembly language and the first high-level languages, FORTRAN and COBOL. Smaller, faster (microseconds), cheaper and more reliable than the first generation; less heat and power, but still air-conditioning. Punched cards for input, printers for output. Examples: IBM 1401 (Nepal's first computer, 2028 BS), IBM 7090, CDC 1604.

Generations of Computer.q: Differentiate between third- and fourth-generation computers in any four points.
What is the fifth generation of computers? Describe its features.
Generations of Computer.r: The fifth generation is the present and future stage in which computers use artificial intelligence to learn, reason and understand natural language (1 mark). Features: AI that learns from data and recognises speech, faces and writing; natural-language input in ordinary words; parallel processing on many processors; ULSI chips with billions of transistors; research on quantum computers and bio-chips; AI languages such as Python and Prolog. Examples: voice assistants, AI chatbots, self-driving cars.

Generations of Computer.q: The Intel 4004 (1971) had 2,300 transistors. Assuming the number doubles every two years, find the expected number in 1991. What is this rule called?
Generations of Computer.r: From 1971 to 1991 is 20 years = 20 ÷ 2 = 10 doublings. Expected number = 2,300 × $2^{10}$ = 2,300 × 1,024 = 2,355,200 (about 2.4 million). The rule is Moore's law. (The real Intel 486 of 1989 had about 1.2 million transistors, so the rule is a good rough guide.)

Explain the fifth generation. What is Moore's law?

Types of Computer.w: the needle moves smoothly; it measures.

Types of Computer.q: An architect needs one powerful computer for 3D models. The best choice is a
Types of Computer.w: a fast single-user machine with a strong graphics card.

Types of Computer.q: Forecasting the monsoon over South Asia needs a
Types of Computer.w: huge parallel calculations need a supercomputer.

Types of Computer.q: A smartphone is a kind of
Write two uses of mainframe computers.
Types of Computer.r: Mainframes serve thousands of users at the same time, so they are used by banks for customer accounts and by airlines and railways for ticket booking (also by governments for census and tax records).

Types of Computer.q: Differentiate between a desktop and a laptop computer.
Types of Computer.r: A desktop is designed to stay on a desk, with a separate monitor, keyboard and system unit, and is cheaper and easier to upgrade. A laptop has the screen, keyboard and battery in one portable unit, so it can be carried and used without mains power.

Types of Computer.q: What are special-purpose computers? Give two examples.
Types of Computer.r: Special-purpose computers are made to do only one particular task; when built into a machine they are called embedded systems. Examples: the computer in a washing machine, a traffic-light controller, an ATM, a digital camera.

Types of Computer.q: Classify computers on the basis of size and explain each type briefly.
Types of Computer.r: Supercomputer: the fastest and most expensive; used for weather and research. Mainframe: large, very powerful, used by thousands of users at once in banks and airlines. Minicomputer: medium-sized and multi-user, used by smaller organisations; today's servers do this job. Microcomputer: a computer built around a microprocessor for one user, such as a desktop, laptop, tablet or smartphone.

Types of Computer.q: Which type of computer would you choose for each, and why:
p: a bank's head office serving all its branches,
a student doing homework at home,
Types of Computer.r: (a) A mainframe (or powerful servers), because thousands of branch users must reach the same accounts at once. (b) A supercomputer, because forecasting needs huge numbers of calculations very fast. (c) A microcomputer — a desktop or laptop — which is cheap and enough for one user. (d) A workstation, a powerful microcomputer with a fast processor and graphics card for design and animation.

Types of Computer.q: A computer that works on continuous data by measuring is
An ECG machine is an example of
Types of Computer.w: it measures the heart's signal and processes it digitally.

Types of Computer.q: The fastest and most expensive type of computer is the
Types of Computer.w: supercomputers lead in speed and cost.

Types of Computer.q: A bank uses a large, reliable computer that serves thousands of users at once. It is a
Types of Computer.w: a mainframe serves thousands of users.

Types of Computer.q: The speed of a supercomputer is measured in
A powerful single-user computer for 3D design and video editing is a
Which of these is a general-purpose computer?
Types of Computer.w: a laptop can run any program.

Types of Computer.q: The PDP-11 is an example of a
Differentiate between analog and digital computers in two points.
Types of Computer.r: An analog computer works on continuous data and measures; a digital computer works on discrete data (0 and 1) and counts. Analog results are approximate; digital results are exact. (Also: analog has little memory, digital has large memory.)

Types of Computer.q: What is a hybrid computer? Give two examples.
Types of Computer.r: A hybrid computer combines analog and digital features: it measures continuous quantities and then processes and displays them digitally. Examples: ECG machine, ICU patient monitor, petrol-pump dispenser.

Types of Computer.q: What is a mainframe computer? Where is it used?
Types of Computer.r: A mainframe is a large, powerful, very reliable computer that serves hundreds or thousands of users at the same time. It is used by banks, insurance companies, airlines, railways and large government offices.

Types of Computer.q: What is a microcomputer? Why is it so popular?
Types of Computer.r: A microcomputer is a small, low-cost computer with a single microprocessor as its CPU, used by one person at a time (a PC). It is popular because it is cheap, small, easy to use and runs millions of programs for study, work and entertainment.

Types of Computer.q: Differentiate between a laptop and a desktop computer.
Types of Computer.r: A desktop stays on a desk, has a separate system unit and needs mains power; a laptop is portable, has everything in one folding case and runs on a battery. A desktop gives more power for the money and is easier to upgrade; a laptop can be used anywhere.

Types of Computer.q: What is a workstation? Who uses it?
Types of Computer.r: A workstation is a powerful single-user microcomputer with a fast multi-core processor, large RAM and a professional graphics card. It is used by engineers, architects, animators, video editors and scientists.

Types of Computer.q: What is an embedded system? Give two examples.
Types of Computer.r: An embedded system is a special-purpose computer built into another machine to control it. Examples: the controller of a washing machine or microwave oven, an ATM, a car's airbag computer, a traffic-light controller.

Types of Computer.q: A supercomputer does $2 \times 10^{18}$ calculations per second and a laptop $10^{12}$. How many seconds would the laptop take to do the supercomputer's work of one second?
What is a hybrid computer? Explain with three examples how it combines analog and digital features.
Types of Computer.r: A hybrid computer combines an analog part that measures continuous quantities with a digital part that calculates, stores and displays (1 mark). ECG machine: measures the heart's electrical signal (analog) and displays and prints it as a trace with values (digital). ICU monitor: measures heart rate, blood pressure and oxygen (analog) and shows exact numbers and sounds alarms (digital). Petrol-pump dispenser: measures the flow of fuel (analog) and calculates and shows litres and rupees (digital).

Types of Computer.q: Differentiate between general-purpose and special-purpose computers in four points.
Describe any four types of microcomputer.
Types of Computer.r: Any four. Desktop: stays on a desk; separate system unit, monitor, keyboard and mouse; powerful for its price; school labs and offices. Laptop: portable, all parts in one folding case with a battery; study and office work anywhere. Tablet: flat, light, touch screen; reading, videos, classes. Smartphone: a phone that runs apps on Android or iOS; calls, payments, photos, GPS. Workstation: powerful single-user computer with a strong processor, large RAM and graphics card; 3D design, video editing, engineering.

Types of Computer.q: A hospital wants
p: a computer for its doctors to read patient records on ward rounds,
a machine to monitor patients in the ICU,
a computer for the billing counter, and
a powerful system to analyse thousands of brain scans for research. Suggest a suitable computer for each, with a reason.
Types of Computer.r: (a) A tablet (or laptop): light and portable, so doctors carry it from bed to bed. (b) A hybrid computer (ICU monitor): it measures heart rate, pressure and oxygen continuously and shows exact values and alarms. (c) A desktop computer with a receipt printer: it stays at the counter and is cheap and reliable. (d) A workstation or a supercomputer/server cluster, depending on size: analysing thousands of scans needs very high processing power and parallel processing.

Types of Computer.q: Classify computers by size. Explain each type with its uses and examples.
Classify computers by working principle and by purpose. Differentiate analog, digital and hybrid computers.

Computer Software.w: each device needs its own driver.

Computer Software.w: it maintains files, so it is a utility.

Computer Software.w: an interpreter works line by line.

Computer Software.w: Windows must be licensed; the others are open source.

Computer Software.q: The safe way to remove a program from Windows 11 is to
o: use Settings → Apps → Installed apps → Uninstall
Computer Software.w: deleting icons or folders leaves the program or breaks it.

Computer Software.q: What is a device driver? Why is it needed?
Computer Software.r: A device driver is a small program that lets the operating system communicate with one particular hardware device, such as a printer, webcam or graphics card. Without the right driver the device does not work, or works badly.

Computer Software.q: What are utility programs? Give two examples.
Computer Software.r: Utility programs are system programs that maintain, protect and tidy the computer. Examples: antivirus, backup software, file compression (WinRAR, 7-Zip), Disk Cleanup.

Computer Software.q: Differentiate between packaged and tailor-made software.
Computer Software.r: Packaged software is ready-made for many users and sold or given in the market, such as MS Office or VLC. Tailor-made (customised) software is built for the needs of one organisation, such as a school's result system or a bank's account system.

Computer Software.q: Differentiate between freeware and shareware.
Computer Software.r: Freeware can be used free of cost for ever, but its source code is not given (for example Google Chrome, Adobe Acrobat Reader). Shareware can be tried free for a limited time or with limited features, after which the user must pay (for example WinRAR's trial).

Computer Software.q: Explain the four kinds of system software.
Computer Software.r: Operating system: manages all hardware and software and provides the user interface (Windows, Linux). Device drivers: let the OS control each device. Utility programs: maintain and protect the computer (antivirus, backup, compression). Language processors: translate programs into machine code — assembler, compiler and interpreter.

Computer Software.q: Explain proprietary and open-source software with examples. Why is software piracy wrong?
Computer Software.r: Proprietary software is owned by a company; users buy a licence to use it, and the source code is secret and may not be changed or shared (MS Windows, MS Office, Adobe Photoshop). Open-source software is free to use, and its source code is open for anyone to study, change and share (Linux, LibreOffice, GIMP, Firefox). Piracy — copying or using software without a licence — is wrong because it is theft of the makers' work, it is a crime, and pirated copies often carry viruses.

Computer Software.q: A set of programs that tells the hardware what to do is called
Computer Software.w: software tells the hardware what to do.

Computer Software.q: Which of these is system software?
Computer Software.w: the operating system is system software.

Computer Software.w: each device needs its own driver.

Computer Software.q: Which is a utility program?
Computer Software.w: antivirus protects the computer; the others are applications.

Computer Software.w: an interpreter works line by line.

What is software? Write two reasons why it is important.
Computer Software.r: Software is a set of programs that tells the computer's hardware what to do. It is important because hardware cannot work without it, and because it makes the computer versatile — the same machine does many tasks by running different software. (Also: lets people use the computer easily; solves problems in every field.)

Computer Software.q: Differentiate between system software and application software.
Computer Software.r: System software controls and manages the hardware and runs whenever the computer is on (e.g. Windows, drivers). Application software helps the user do a particular task and runs only when opened (e.g. MS Word, Chrome).

Computer Software.q: What is a utility program? Name any three.
Computer Software.r: A utility program is system software that maintains, protects or improves the computer and its data. Examples: antivirus (Microsoft Defender), file compression (7-Zip), disk cleanup, backup, Task Manager.

Computer Software.q: Differentiate between a compiler and an interpreter in two points.
Computer Software.r: A compiler translates the whole program at once and makes a separate machine-code file; an interpreter translates and runs one line at a time and makes no file. A compiler lists all errors after translating; an interpreter stops at the first error. (E.g. C uses a compiler; Python an interpreter.)

Computer Software.q: Differentiate between packaged and tailor-made software, with one example of each.
Computer Software.r: Packaged software is ready-made for many users with common needs and is cheaper, e.g. Microsoft Excel. Tailor-made software is written for one organization's own needs and is costlier, e.g. a school's own result-processing system.

Computer Software.q: What is open-source software? Give two examples.
Computer Software.r: Open-source software is software whose source code is open for anyone to use, read, change and share under its licence; it is usually free. Examples: Linux, LibreOffice, Firefox, VLC, Python (any two).

Computer Software.q: Write the steps to uninstall a program in Windows 11.
Why should software be updated regularly? Give two reasons.
Computer Software.r: Updates fix bugs (mistakes) in programs and close security holes that viruses and hackers use; they also add new features and keep the software working with new hardware and files.

Computer Software.q: What is system software? Explain its four types with examples.
Computer Software.r: System software is the group of programs that controls and manages the hardware and provides a base for application software (1 mark). Operating system: manages hardware, memory, files and programs and gives the user an interface — Windows 11, Linux, Android. Device drivers: let the OS control one device — a printer or graphics card driver. Utility programs: maintain and protect the computer — antivirus, backup, disk cleanup, 7-Zip. Language processors: translate programs into machine language — assembler, compiler (C), interpreter (Python).

Computer Software.q: Explain proprietary, freeware, shareware and open-source software with an example of each.
Computer Software.r: Proprietary: owned by a company, code secret, must buy a licence, cannot copy or change — Microsoft Windows, MS Office. Freeware: free of cost to use, but code closed and cannot be changed — Google Chrome, Zoom. Shareware: free for a trial period or with limited features, then must be bought — WinRAR, Internet Download Manager. Open source: source code open; anyone may use, change and share it, usually free — Linux, LibreOffice, Firefox.

Computer Software.q: Describe how to install software safely on a Windows computer, and give two precautions.
Computer Software.r: Steps: check the system requirements; download from the Microsoft Store or the maker's official website; run the installer; at the "allow this app to make changes" prompt check the publisher and click Yes; accept the licence; choose Custom setup and untick unwanted extra programs; click Install, then Finish. Precautions (any two): never install cracked or pirated software; download only from official sources; keep the antivirus on; check free disk space first; be careful of extra toolbars and offers.

Computer Software.q: A hospital wants
p: to keep its own patient, ward and billing records in its own format,
to protect its computers from viruses and
to run its new X-ray printer. Name the type of software needed for each, with an example.
Computer Software.r: (a) Packaged application software, a word processor — MS Word or LibreOffice Writer. (b) Tailor-made application software — a hospital management system written for that hospital. (c) Utility software, an antivirus — Microsoft Defender or Kaspersky. (d) System software, a device driver — the X-ray printer's driver from its maker.

Operating System.q: Differentiate between CUI and GUI operating systems.
Operating System.r: In a CUI (character user interface) the user types commands, as in MS-DOS or the Linux terminal; it needs commands to be remembered. In a GUI (graphical user interface) the user clicks windows, icons, menus and buttons with a mouse or a finger, as in Windows or Android; it is easy for beginners.

Operating System.q: What is a file extension? Write two examples with the type of file.
Operating System.r: A file extension is the part of a file name after the dot that shows the type of file. Examples:.docx — a Word document;.jpg — a photograph;.mp3 — a sound file;.exe — a program (any two).

Operating System.q: Differentiate between copying and moving a file, with the shortcut keys.
Operating System.r: Copying makes a duplicate in the new place and leaves the original where it was (Ctrl + C, then Ctrl + V). Moving takes the file to the new place and removes it from the old one (Ctrl + X, then Ctrl + V).

Operating System.q: What is the Recycle Bin? How can a file be restored from it?
Operating System.r: The Recycle Bin is a folder where Windows keeps files deleted from the hard disk, so that they can be recovered. To restore a file, open the Recycle Bin, select the file and click Restore; it returns to its old folder. (Files deleted with Shift + Delete, or from a pen drive, skip the Recycle Bin.)

Operating System.q: Explain single-user and multi-user, and desktop and mobile operating systems, with examples.
Operating System.r: A single-user OS lets one person use the computer at a time (Windows 11 Home). A multi-user OS lets many users work on it at the same time, usually over a network (Linux servers, UNIX). A desktop OS runs on desktops and laptops (Windows, macOS, Linux). A mobile OS runs on smartphones and tablets and is designed for touch screens (Android, iOS).

Define operating system. Name two examples.
Operating System.r: An operating system is system software that controls and manages all the hardware and software of a computer and provides an interface between the user and the computer. Examples: Windows 11, Linux, macOS, Android, iOS (any two).

Operating System.q: Write any four functions of an operating system.
Operating System.r: Any four: process management (runs programs, multitasking); memory management; file management; device management through drivers; security and user accounts; providing the user interface; booting.

Operating System.q: Differentiate between CUI and GUI.
Operating System.r: In a CUI the user types commands and sees only text, e.g. MS-DOS; in a GUI the user clicks windows, icons and menus, e.g. Windows. A CUI needs remembered commands and little memory; a GUI is easy to learn but needs more memory and processing power.

Operating System.q: Differentiate between single-user and multi-user operating systems.
Operating System.r: A single-user OS lets one user work at a time, e.g. Windows 11 Home on a PC. A multi-user OS lets many users work on one computer at the same time through terminals or a network, keeping their work separate, e.g. Linux or UNIX servers.

Operating System.q: What is a mobile operating system? Name two.
Operating System.r: A mobile operating system runs on smartphones and tablets; it is designed for touch, small screens and battery saving, and uses the camera, GPS and mobile network. Examples: Android and iOS.

Operating System.q: What is a dialog box? Name any three of its controls.
Operating System.r: A dialog box is a small window in which a program asks the user for information or a choice before carrying out a command. Controls (any three): tabs, text box, drop-down list, check box, option button, spin box, command buttons (OK, Cancel, Apply).

Operating System.q: Differentiate between a file and a folder.
Operating System.r: A file is a named collection of related data, such as a document or photo, e.g. essay.docx. A folder is a named container that holds files and other folders to keep them organized, e.g. Documents.

Operating System.q: Write the difference between copying and moving a file.
Operating System.r: Copying (Ctrl + C, Ctrl + V) keeps the original and makes a duplicate in the new place; moving (Ctrl + X, Ctrl + V) removes the file from the old place and puts it only in the new place.

Operating System.q: What is the Recycle Bin? How can a deleted file be restored?
Operating System.r: The Recycle Bin is a special folder that keeps files deleted from the computer's own drives so that they can be restored. To restore: open the Recycle Bin, select the file and click Restore the selected items (or right-click → Restore); it returns to its original folder.

Operating System.q: What is an operating system? Explain any three functions.
Operating System.r: An operating system is system software that manages the hardware and software and provides the user interface (1 mark). Any three, explained: process management — starts and stops programs and shares the CPU among them, so several run at once (multitasking); memory management — allocates RAM to each program and frees it when the program closes; file management — creates, saves, names, copies, moves, deletes and finds files and folders; device management — controls input and output devices through their drivers; security — user accounts, passwords and permissions.

Word Processing.q: Write any four features of a word processor and name two word processors.
Word Processing.r: Any four: typing and editing text; formatting text and paragraphs; spelling and grammar checking; inserting tables, pictures and shapes; headers, footers and page numbers; mail merge; saving and printing. Word processors: Microsoft Word, LibreOffice Writer, Google Docs (any two).

Word Processing.q: Differentiate between Save and Save As.
Word Processing.r: Save (Ctrl + S) stores the document under its present name and place; the first time, it asks for a name. Save As (F12 in Word) saves a copy under a new name, in a new place or in another format, keeping the old file as it was.

Word Processing.q: Differentiate between cut and copy. Write their shortcut keys.
Word Processing.r: Cut (Ctrl + X) removes the selected text and keeps it on the clipboard to be pasted elsewhere; copy (Ctrl + C) keeps the text in its place and puts a copy on the clipboard. Both are pasted with Ctrl + V.

Word Processing.q: What is Find and Replace? Write its shortcut keys.
Word Processing.r: Find (Ctrl + F) searches the document for a word or phrase. Replace (Ctrl + H) finds a word and changes it to another, one at a time or all at once with Replace All — for example changing every "Kathmandu" to "Lalitpur".

Word Processing.q: Explain font formatting, paragraph formatting, bullets and numbering, and page layout.
Word Processing.r: Font formatting: changing the font type, size, colour and style (bold, italic, underline) of characters. Paragraph formatting: alignment (left, centre, right, justify), line spacing, indentation and space before and after. Bullets and numbering: making lists that start with symbols or numbers. Page layout: margins, orientation (portrait or landscape), page size (A4) and columns.

Word Processing.q: What are header, footer and page numbers? How can a table and a picture be inserted into a document?
Word Processing.r: A header is text printed at the top of every page and a footer at the bottom (such as the school name or a date); page numbers number the pages automatically (Insert → Header, Footer, Page Number). A table is inserted with Insert → Table, choosing the number of rows and columns; a picture with Insert → Pictures, choosing the image file, then resizing it by its corner handles.

Word Processing.q: What is a word processor? Name two examples.
Word Processing.r: A word processor is application software used to create, edit, format, save and print text documents. Examples: Microsoft Word, LibreOffice Writer, Google Docs (any two).

Word Processing.q: Write any four features of a word processor.
Word Processing.r: Any four: word wrap; editing with cut, copy, paste and undo; find and replace; spelling and grammar check; formatting of fonts, paragraphs and pages; tables, pictures and shapes; headers, footers and page numbers; mail merge; saving as PDF; templates.

Word Processing.q: Differentiate between Cut and Copy.
Word Processing.r: Cut (Ctrl + X) removes the selected text and keeps it on the clipboard, so pasting moves it. Copy (Ctrl + C) leaves the text where it is and puts a copy on the clipboard, so pasting duplicates it.

Word Processing.q: Write the steps to find the word "Kathmandu" and replace it with "Lalitpur" everywhere in a document.
Word Processing.r: Press Ctrl + H (Home → Editing → Replace). Type Kathmandu in Find what and Lalitpur in Replace with; under More, tick Find whole words only if needed; click Replace All, then OK.

Word Processing.q: Write the steps to insert page numbers at the bottom of every page in Word.
Word Processing.r: Insert tab → Page Number → Bottom of Page → choose a style such as Plain Number 2; then click Close Header and Footer.

Word Processing.q: Write the steps to insert a table of 4 columns and 6 rows.
Word Processing.r: Place the cursor; Insert → Table → Insert Table…; type 4 in Number of columns and 6 in Number of rows; click OK. (In Writer: Table → Insert Table.)

Word Processing.q: What is meant by text wrapping? Name two wrapping options.
Word Processing.r: Text wrapping decides how the text of the document flows around a picture or shape. Options (any two): In Line with Text, Square, Tight, Top and Bottom, Behind Text, In Front of Text.

Word Processing.q: Write the shortcut keys for: bold, centre alignment, paste and print.
Word Processing.r: Bold: Ctrl + B; centre: Ctrl + E; paste: Ctrl + V; print: Ctrl + P.

Word Processing.q: Explain any four parts of the Microsoft Word window with a labelled sketch.
Word Processing.r: Sketch as in Figure 1. Any four: Title bar — shows the document's name and the program. Quick Access Toolbar — Save, Undo, Redo always at hand. Ribbon — tabs (Home, Insert, Layout …) with groups of commands. Ruler — shows and sets margins, indents and tab stops. Document area — where text is typed; the insertion point marks the typing position. Scroll bars — move through the document. Status bar — page number, word count and language; zoom slider — enlarge or shrink the view.

Word Processing.q: Explain any four types of paragraph formatting with examples.
Word Processing.r: Any four. Alignment: the position of lines between the margins — left, centre (a title), right (a date), justify (a report). Line spacing: the space between lines — 1.0 for normal text, 1.5 or 2.0 for drafts. Indentation: moving a paragraph in from the margin — first-line indent in a story, hanging indent in a list of references. Spacing before and after: space between paragraphs. Bullets and numbering: lists of points or steps. Borders and shading: a box or background colour behind a paragraph.

Word Processing.q: A 20-page document is printed with Pages: 1-5, 11, 15-16 and Copies: 4 on both sides of the paper. How many pages print per copy, how many printed pages in all, and how many sheets are used? Show your working.
Word Processing.r: 1-5 gives pages 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 (5 pages); 11 (1 page); 15-16 gives 15 and 16 (2 pages). Pages per copy = 5 + 1 + 2 = 8. Printed pages = 8 × 4 = 32. Both sides: 8 ÷ 2 = 4 sheets per copy, so 4 × 4 = 16 sheets.

Spreadsheet Software.q: Differentiate between relative and absolute cell references with examples.

Spreadsheet Software.q: The price of an item is in A2 and the VAT rate 13% is in cell E1. Write the formula in B2 for the VAT, which can be copied down for items in A3 to A10, and explain why it must use an absolute reference. Then find the VAT on Rs 2,500.
Spreadsheet Software.r: In B2: =A2*$E$1 (or =A2*$E$1/100 if E1 holds 13 rather than 13%). When the formula is copied down, A2 must change to A3, A4 … for each item, but every row must still use the one VAT rate in E1; the dollar signs keep $E$1 fixed. Without them the copied formulas would point to E2, E3 …, which are empty, giving 0. VAT on Rs 2,500 = 2,500 × 13 ÷ 100 = Rs 325.

Spreadsheet Software.q: Define cell, cell address and range with an example of each.

Spreadsheet Software.q: Differentiate between a workbook and a worksheet.
Spreadsheet Software.r: A workbook is the whole spreadsheet file (e.g. Marks.xlsx); a worksheet is one grid of rows and columns inside it, chosen by a sheet tab. One workbook can hold many worksheets.

Spreadsheet Software.q: Differentiate between a formula and a function, with an example of each.
Spreadsheet Software.r: A formula is any calculation the user writes, beginning with =, e.g. =B2+C2+D2. A function is a built-in, named formula, e.g. =SUM(B2:D2). Functions can be used inside formulas.

Spreadsheet Software.q: What is AutoFill? Write what appears when "Monday" is filled down three cells.
Spreadsheet Software.r: AutoFill copies cell contents or continues a series when the fill handle is dragged. Filling "Monday" down three cells gives Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday.

Spreadsheet Software.q: Differentiate between relative and absolute cell references.
Spreadsheet Software.r: A relative reference (B2) changes when the formula is copied, by the number of rows and columns moved. An absolute reference ($B$2) stays fixed on the same cell when copied, e.g. a VAT rate in one cell.

Spreadsheet Software.q: Write an IF function that shows "Eligible" if the age in B2 is 16 or more and "Not eligible" otherwise.
Differentiate between sorting and filtering.
Spreadsheet Software.r: Sorting rearranges all the rows in ascending or descending order of a column; filtering shows only the rows that meet a condition and hides the others without changing their order.

Spreadsheet Software.q: Which chart would you use to show

Spreadsheet Software.r: (a) A line chart, because temperature changes over time and a line shows the trend. (b) A pie chart, because the votes are parts of one whole (total votes).

MAX(range) gives the largest: =MAX(B2:B6) = 90. MIN(range) gives the smallest: =MIN(B2:B6) = 42. COUNT(range) counts cells with numbers: =COUNT(B2:B6) = 5. Spreadsheet Software.r: Column chart: vertical bars comparing separate items — marks in each subject. Line chart: points joined by a line showing change over time — temperature through a week. Spreadsheet Software.q: The marks of a student out of 100 are 64, 38, 75, 81 and 57 in B2:F2. Write formulas for the total, the percentage (out of 500), the highest and lowest marks, and a result that is "Pass" only if every mark is at least 40. Give each result.
Spreadsheet Software.r: Total: =SUM(B2:F2) = 64 + 38 + 75 + 81 + 57 = 315. Percentage: =SUM(B2:F2)/500*100 (or the total's cell /500100) = 63. Highest: =MAX(B2:F2) = 81. Lowest: =MIN(B2:F2) = 38. Result: =IF(MIN(B2:F2)>=40,"Pass","Fail") gives Fail*, because the lowest mark, 38, is below 40.

Presentation Software.q: What is presentation software? Name two examples.
Presentation Software.r: Presentation software is application software used to create slides containing text, pictures, charts, audio and video and to show them one by one to an audience. Examples: Microsoft PowerPoint, LibreOffice Impress, Google Slides.

Presentation Software.q: What is a placeholder? What is a slide layout?
Presentation Software.r: A placeholder is a dotted box on a slide that holds a title, text, a picture or a chart ("Click to add title"). A slide layout is the arrangement of placeholders on a slide, such as Title Slide, Title and Content, or Two Content.

Presentation Software.q: What is a slide master? Why is it useful?
Presentation Software.r: The slide master (View → Slide Master) is the top slide that stores the design of all slides — background, fonts, colours, logo and placeholder positions. A change made on it appears on every slide at once, which saves time and keeps the slides consistent.

Presentation Software.q: Write two ways to start a slide show and the keys used.
Presentation Software.r: Press F5 (or Slide Show → From Beginning) to start from the first slide; press Shift + F5 (or From Current Slide) to start from the slide on screen. Esc ends the show.

Presentation Software.q: Write the steps to make a five-slide presentation about your school with a title slide, a picture, a chart and a transition, and to run it.
Presentation Software.r: (1) Open PowerPoint → Blank Presentation, choose a theme on the Design tab. (2) Slide 1 (Title Slide layout): type the school's name and address. (3) Add slides with Home → New Slide: history, facilities (Insert → Pictures, the school photo), results (Insert → Chart, a column chart of pass percentages), and a thank-you slide. (4) Apply a transition from the Transitions tab → Apply To All; save as school.pptx; run with F5.

Presentation Software.q: Write any four rules for designing an effective presentation.
Presentation Software.r: Any four: use one simple theme throughout; keep about six lines of six words per slide (the 6 × 6 rule); use a large, clear font (at least 24 points) with strong contrast between text and background; use pictures and charts instead of long paragraphs; use only a few, gentle animations and transitions; check spelling; end with a summary.

Presentation Software.q: Which of these is presentation software?
The default file extension of a PowerPoint presentation is
A dotted box on a slide that shows Click to add title is a
The effect when one slide changes to the next is a
An animation that makes an object appear on the slide belongs to the group
The view that shows small thumbnails of all slides for reordering is
Pressing F5 in PowerPoint
o: starts the show from the first slide
Presentation Software.w: F5 runs the show from the beginning.

Presentation Software.q: Write any four features of presentation software.
Presentation Software.r: Any four: layouts and themes; placeholders; pictures, tables, charts, audio and video; transitions and animations; several views; slide master; speaker notes and Presenter View; rehearse timings; export to PDF or video.

Presentation Software.q: Define slide layout and theme.
Presentation Software.r: A slide layout is the arrangement of placeholders on a slide, such as Title and Content. A theme is a ready-made design of background, colours, fonts and effects applied to all the slides.

Presentation Software.q: Differentiate between a transition and an animation.
Presentation Software.r: A transition is the effect when moving from one slide to the next and is set on the Transitions tab; an animation is an effect on an object (text, picture) within a slide and is set on the Animations tab. A slide has one transition but may have many animations.

Presentation Software.q: Write the steps to apply the same transition to all slides.
Presentation Software.r: Select a slide → Transitions tab → click an effect such as Fade → set Effect Options and Duration → click Apply To All.

Presentation Software.q: Write the steps to insert a video stored on the computer into a slide.
Presentation Software.r: Select the slide → Insert tab → Video → This Device → find and select the video file → Insert; then set Start (On Click or Automatically) on the Playback tab.

Presentation Software.q: What is the slide master? Why is it useful?
Presentation Software.r: The slide master is the top master slide that stores the design of the presentation — background, fonts, colours, placeholder positions, logo and footer. It is useful because a change made on it appears on every slide at once, saving time and keeping all slides consistent.

Presentation Software.q: Name four views of PowerPoint and write the use of any two.
Presentation Software.r: Normal, Outline View, Slide Sorter, Notes Page, Reading View, Slide Show (any four). Normal — editing one slide; Slide Sorter — reordering and deleting slides; Notes Page — writing speaker notes; Slide Show — presenting full screen (any two uses).

Presentation Software.q: Write the keys used to start a slide show from the beginning, start from the current slide, show a black screen and end the show.
Presentation Software.r: F5 — from the beginning; Shift + F5 — from the current slide; B — black screen; Esc — end the show.

Presentation Software.q: Write any four rules for making effective slides.
Presentation Software.r: Any four: one idea per slide; keywords not paragraphs (6 × 6 rule); large type (title 36–44 pt, body at least 24 pt); strong contrast between text and background; one consistent theme; relevant pictures and charts; few animations; check spelling; rehearse.

Presentation Software.q: Write the steps to create a four-slide presentation on "Tourism in Nepal" with a title slide, a picture, a table and a transition on every slide.
Presentation Software.r: Open PowerPoint → Blank Presentation. Slide 1 (Title Slide): type Tourism in Nepal and your name. Ctrl + M for slide 2 (Title and Content): type four points about tourist places. Ctrl + M for slide 3: Insert → Pictures → This Device → choose a photo of Pokhara → Insert, and add a title. Ctrl + M for slide 4: Insert → Table → 3 columns × 4 rows, type the places, districts and attractions. Design → choose a theme. Transitions → Fade → Apply To All. Save (Ctrl + S) as Tourism in Nepal.pptx and press F5 to check.

Presentation Software.q: Explain the four types of animation effect and the three ways an animation can start.
Presentation Software.r: Entrance (green) — the object appears, e.g. Fly In, Fade. Emphasis (yellow) — draws attention while visible, e.g. Pulse, Spin. Exit (red) — the object leaves, e.g. Fly Out, Disappear. Motion Paths — the object moves along a line, arc or custom path. Start options: On Click — waits for a click; With Previous — starts together with the previous effect; After Previous — starts when the previous effect ends.

Presentation Software.q: Describe any four slide views with the use of each.
Presentation Software.r: Any four. Normal — one slide large with thumbnails and notes, for creating and editing. Outline — the text of all slides as an outline, for writing content. Slide Sorter — thumbnails of all slides, for reordering, deleting, hiding and setting transitions. Notes Page — the slide with its notes, for preparing the speaker's notes. Reading View — the show in a window, for checking. Slide Show — full screen, for presenting.

Explain transitions and animations and the rules of an effective presentation.

Web Page Design.q: Differentiate between a web page and a website.
Web Page Design.r: A web page is a single document on the World Wide Web, written in HTML and opened in a browser. A website is a collection of related web pages under one domain name, linked together, such as all the pages of neb.gov.np.

Web Page Design.q: What is a URL? Name its parts in the example address https://www.myschool.edu.np/results.html.
Web Page Design.r: A URL (Uniform Resource Locator) is the full address of a resource on the web. In https://www.myschool.edu.np/results.html: https is the protocol, www.myschool.edu.np is the domain name (the server), and /results.html is the path to the page on that server.

Web Page Design.q: What does CSS stand for?

Web Page Design.q: Which of the following is NOT a valid semantic HTML5 element?

Web Page Design.q: What is the purpose of the DOCTYPE declaration in an HTML document?

Information and Communication Technology.q: ICT stands for
Information and Communication Technology.w: Information and Communication Technology.

Information and Communication Technology.q: The rules and steps for using an ICT system correctly and safely form its
Information and Communication Technology.w: procedures are the rules and steps people follow.

Information and Communication Technology.q: A geostationary satellite orbits the Earth at a height of about
Information and Communication Technology.w: about 35,786 km above the equator.

Information and Communication Technology.q: Nepal's first satellite, NepaliSat-1, was launched in
Information and Communication Technology.w: launched in 2019.

Information and Communication Technology.q: To send a copy of an e-mail without the other receivers seeing that address, put it in
Information and Communication Technology.w: blind carbon copy.

Information and Communication Technology.q: A citizen renewing a document through a government website is an example of
Information and Communication Technology.w: government to citizen.

Information and Communication Technology.q: Differentiate between the Internet and the World Wide Web.
Information and Communication Technology.r: The Internet is the worldwide network of networks — the cables, routers and computers joined by TCP/IP. The World Wide Web is one service that runs on the Internet: the collection of linked web pages opened in a browser. E-mail and video calls also use the Internet but are not the Web.

Information and Communication Technology.q: What do To, Cc and Bcc mean in an e-mail?
Information and Communication Technology.r: To: the main receivers of the message. Cc (carbon copy): others who get a copy; every receiver can see their addresses. Bcc (blind carbon copy): receivers whose addresses are hidden from all the others.

Information and Communication Technology.q: What is cloud storage? Give two examples.
Information and Communication Technology.r: Cloud storage keeps files on servers on the Internet instead of on your own device, so they can be opened from any device and are safe if a phone is lost. Examples: Google Drive, Microsoft OneDrive, Dropbox, iCloud.

Information and Communication Technology.q: What is the digital divide? Write two ways to reduce it.
Information and Communication Technology.r: The digital divide is the gap between people who have devices, the Internet and the skills to use them and those who do not — for example, in the 2021 census 45.7% of households in municipalities but only 21.5% in rural municipalities had the Internet. Ways to reduce it: extend cheap broadband and mobile data to rural areas; give schools computers and teach digital skills (also: community information centres, local-language content).

Information and Communication Technology.q: What is e-governance? Explain G2C, G2B and G2G with Nepali examples.
Information and Communication Technology.r: E-governance is the use of ICT by the government to give its services and information to people quickly and openly (1 mark). G2C (government to citizen): the Nagarik App, launched in 2021, gives citizens their PAN, driving licence and other records on the phone. G2B (government to business): companies file taxes and register online with government offices. G2G (government to government): offices share records over the government network instead of on paper (3 marks).

Information and Communication Technology.q: Write two advantages and two disadvantages of ICT.
Information and Communication Technology.r: Advantages: quick and cheap communication across the world; online banking, shopping and learning from home; faster government services. Disadvantages: cyber crime, fraud and loss of privacy; addiction and health problems; the digital divide leaves poorer and rural people behind (any two of each).

Information and Communication Technology.q: ICT stands for
Information and Communication Technology.w: information and communication technology.

Information and Communication Technology.q: A radio broadcast is an example of
Information and Communication Technology.w: listeners receive but cannot reply through the radio.

Information and Communication Technology.q: The area served by one mobile tower is called a
Information and Communication Technology.w: each tower serves one cell; hence "cellular" network.

Information and Communication Technology.q: The signal sent from a ground station up to a satellite is the
Information and Communication Technology.w: up is the uplink; the signal coming down is the downlink.

Information and Communication Technology.q: Radio Nepal was established in
Information and Communication Technology.w: 20 Chaitra 2007 BS (2 April 1951).

Information and Communication Technology.q: Which Internet service keeps your files on a company's servers so that you can open them from any device?
Information and Communication Technology.w: e.g. Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox.

Information and Communication Technology.q: In an e-mail, the addresses that other receivers cannot see are written in
Information and Communication Technology.w: Bcc means blind carbon copy.

Information and Communication Technology.q: The gap between people who can use ICT and those who cannot is the
Information and Communication Technology.w: the digital divide.

Information and Communication Technology.q: Define ICT. Name any four components of an ICT system.
Information and Communication Technology.r: ICT is the use of computers, telecommunication equipment, networks and software to collect, store, process, send and receive information. Components (any four): hardware, software, data, network, people, procedures.

Information and Communication Technology.q: Write any two differences between radio and television.
Information and Communication Technology.r: Radio carries sound only, while television carries moving pictures and sound. A radio set is cheap and runs on batteries, so it reaches remote villages; a TV set costs more and needs more power. (Any two.)

Information and Communication Technology.q: What is a communication satellite? Write any two uses of satellites.
Information and Communication Technology.r: A communication satellite is a machine in orbit that receives signals from a ground station (uplink), strengthens them and sends them back to a wide area of the Earth (downlink). Uses (any two): satellite TV (DTH), satellite phones, Internet in remote places (VSAT), GPS navigation, weather forecasting.

Information and Communication Technology.q: Differentiate between the Internet and the WWW.
Information and Communication Technology.r: The Internet is the worldwide network of computer networks — the cables, devices and rules — and carries every service. The WWW is a collection of linked web pages that is only one service running on the Internet; e-mail and video calls use the Internet without using the Web.

Information and Communication Technology.q: What is video conferencing? Name two programs used for it.
Information and Communication Technology.r: Video conferencing is a live meeting over the Internet in which people at different places see and hear each other at the same time using cameras and microphones. Programs (any two): Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Jitsi Meet.

Information and Communication Technology.q: What is cloud storage? Write one advantage and one disadvantage of it.
Information and Communication Technology.r: Cloud storage is a service that keeps your files on a company's servers on the Internet so that you can open and share them from any device. Advantage: the files are safe even if your phone or computer is lost (or: they can be opened anywhere and shared). Disadvantage: you need the Internet to reach them (or: your data is held by another company, so privacy depends on its security).

Information and Communication Technology.q: What is e-governance? Give two examples of e-governance in Nepal.
Information and Communication Technology.r: e-Governance is the use of ICT by the government to give services and information to citizens, businesses and its own offices. Examples (any two): the Nagarik App, the online passport form, SEE and NEB results online, online tax filing with the Inland Revenue Department, the Hello Sarkar complaint service.

Information and Communication Technology.q: Name any two digital payment systems of Nepal and write one safety rule for using them.
Information and Communication Technology.r: Any two of eSewa, Khalti, IME Pay, Fonepay QR, connectIPS, mobile banking. Safety rule: never tell anyone your OTP or MPIN (or: use only the official app, keep the phone locked, check the amount and the receiver before confirming).

Information and Communication Technology.q: What is the digital divide? Write any two ways to reduce it.
Information and Communication Technology.r: The digital divide is the gap between people who have devices, the Internet and the skill to use ICT and people who do not. Ways (any two): cheaper data and devices; more towers and fibre in rural areas; community ICT centres and free Wi-Fi in schools and libraries; computer classes for adults; content in Nepali and local languages.

Information and Communication Technology.q: A 600 MB video is uploaded on a 40 Mbps connection. Find the shortest time the upload can take.
Information and Communication Technology.r: 600 MB × 8 = 4,800 Mb. Time = 4,800 ÷ 40 = 120 seconds = 2 minutes.

Information and Communication Technology.q: What is ICT? Explain any three uses of ICT in Nepal with an example of each.
Information and Communication Technology.r: ICT is the use of computers, telecommunication equipment, networks and software to collect, store, process, send and receive information (1 mark). Uses (any three, 1 mark each): Education — online classes, digital textbooks and results; e.g. Sikai Chautari lessons and SEE results published online. Banking — mobile banking and digital wallets let people pay and send money from a phone; e.g. paying a shop with Khalti or eSewa by QR code. Government (e-governance) — services without queues; e.g. the Nagarik App for citizenship, PAN and police reports. Health — telemedicine lets a doctor in a city advise a health post by video call.

Information and Communication Technology.q: Describe any four communication technologies, giving an example of each from Nepal.
Information and Communication Technology.r: (Any four, 1 mark each.) Telephone (landline): turns the voice into an electrical signal that travels by wire through an exchange to the other telephone; two-way; e.g. a Nepal Telecom landline. Mobile phone: uses radio waves to the tower of its cell, and the towers are joined through the mobile exchange; carries calls, SMS and data; e.g. Nepal Telecom and Ncell. Radio: sends sound by radio waves from a transmitter to many receivers; one-way, cheap, reaches remote villages; e.g. Radio Nepal (2007 BS) and community FM stations. Television: sends moving pictures and sound by antenna, cable, satellite or the Internet; e.g. NTV and DishHome.

Information and Communication Technology.q: What is the digital divide? Explain its causes in Nepal and suggest two ways to bridge it.
Information and Communication Technology.r: The digital divide is the gap between people who have access to ICT — devices, the Internet and the skill to use them — and people who do not (1 mark). Causes in Nepal (2 marks): the cost of devices and data; difficult hills and mountains where towers and cables are costly to build; weak electricity in some villages; lack of computer skills, especially among older people; most content is in English. The 2021 census showed Internet in 45.7% of urban but only 21.5% of rural households. Ways to bridge it (1 mark, any two): cheaper data and devices; more towers and fibre in rural areas; community ICT centres and free Wi-Fi in schools and ward offices; computer classes for adults;

Information and Communication Technology.q: What is ICT? Explain eight advantages and seven disadvantages of ICT, and the digital divide.
Explain the use of ICT in Nepal in e-governance, digital payment and e-learning.
Describe the main Internet services.

A fake e-mail that looks like it comes from a bank and asks for your password is
Computer Ethics and Cyber Law.w: phishing "fishes" for passwords with fake messages.

Computer Ethics and Cyber Law.q: Copying an essay from a website and handing it in as your own work is
Computer Ethics and Cyber Law.w: plagiarism; piracy is copying software or media.
